NAME: MARATHON ASHLAND PIPE LINE LLC
NARRATIVE: AT 09:45 A.M. ON AUGUST 20 THE NAUTILUS- OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN NOTICED GAS SEEPING FROM THE BASE OF A 2" WELD-O-LET IN NAUTILUS GARDEN CITY MANIFOLD ON THE 24" PIPING TO THE EXXON GAS PLANT. THE AFFECTED PIPING WAS ISOLATED (DOUBLE-BLOCKED IN BY CLOSING TWO UPSTREAM VALVES AND TWO DOWNSTREAM VALVES) AND THE AFFECTED LINE SECTION (APPROXIMATELY 60 FOOT LINE) WAS BLOWN DOWN. GAS DELIVERY TO THE ADJACENT NEPTUNE PLANT WAS ABLE TO CONTINUE SAFELY. NO PUBLIC OR ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURE WAS CAUSED BY THIS INCIDENT. THE 2" WELD-O-LET WAS LOCATED IN THE NAUTILUS MANIFOLD DOWNSTREAM OF THE EXXON ORIFICE METERS AND IMMEDIATELY UPSTREAM OF THE EXXON CONTROL VALVE (FV 3030). THE 2" WELD-O-LET WAS USED FOR A SAMPLE POINT AND WAS ONE OF THREE 2" WELD-O-LETS ON A 4 FT. LONG 24 IN DIAMETER JOINT OF PIPE. WET MAGNETIC PARTICLE TESTING CONFIRMED THAT THERE IS A CRACK IN THE PARENT PIPE EXTENDING ABOUT 2" ALONG THE PIPE AXIS TO EITHER SIDE OF THE FILLET WELD. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE CRACK IS UNDETERMINED AT THIS TIME. THE SPECIMEN CONTAINING THE CRACK HAS BEEN SENT TO KIEFNER & ASSOCIATES IN COLUMBUS, OHIO FOR FAILURE ANALYSIS. AT THE TIME OF THE RELEASE, IT WAS BELIEVED THAT REPAIR COSTS WOULD BE LESS THAN $50,000. A DETERMINATION WAS MADE ON AUGUST 23, 2002 THAT REPAIR COSTS WOULD EXCEED $50,000 AND THE NRC WAS NOTIFIED.   4-18-03 LABORATORY ANALYSIS OF THE FAILED SPECIMEN INDICATED THAT THE FAILURE WAS DUE TO FATIGUE CRACKING FROM VIBRATION LOADINGS.  THE CRACK INITIATED AT TOE OF FILLET WELD AT A SHARP CORNER BETWEEN THE FIRST PASS OF THE WELDMENT AND THE CARRIER PIPE BODY.  KIEFNER AND ASSOCIATES WAS CONSULTED CONCERNING THE CAUSE CLASSIFICATION OF THIS EVENT.

NARRATIVE: ON TUESDAY NIGHT AT APPROXIMATELY 9:00 PM, A DRIVER FOR THE WATER-HAULING CONTRACTOR (EMS, INC) WAS BURNED BY A FIELD TANK, WHILE WORKING AT A KINDER MORGAN  STORAGE FACILITY LOCATE IN COLUMBUS JCT, 1A (STATION 204).  THE CONTRACTOR WAS DRAINING ON TANK AND WHILE THAT TANK WAS DRAINING HE ATTEMPTED TO USE A PROPANE TORCH TO THAW A VALVE IN PREPARATION FOR DRAINING ANOTHER TANK.  THE CONTRACTOR HAD NOT HOOKED HIS DRAIN HOSE TO THE SECOND TANK AS IT WAS BEING USED AT THE OTHER TANK.  A KINDER MORGAN EMPLOYEE WITNESSED FLAMES ERUPT FROM A 3" DRAIN VALVE DURING THE THAWING PROCESS.  THE FIRE OCCURRED AS A RESULT OF THE CONTRACTOR OPENING THE VALVE ON THE TANK WHILE USING THE TORCH.  THIS ALLOWED A PATH FOR AN IGNITION SOURCE TO ENTER THE TANK AND ALSO CAUSED A SMALL RELEASE OF LIQUID WHICH WAS IGNITED BY THE TORCH.  FAILING TO HOOK UP THE HOSE TO THE SECOND TANK BEFORE ATTEMPTING TO THAW THE VALVE IS AGAINST ACCEPTED PRACTICE.  AND OPENING UP THE VALVE WHILE USING THE TORCH IS A VIOLATION AGAINST THE PROCEDURE SET OUT IN OM 103 - HOT WORK AND AGAINST PROCEDURES REVIEWED IN THE KINDER MORGAN CONTRACTOR SAFETY PROGRAM.  UPON EXTINGUISHING THE FIRE AT THE VALVE, THE CONTRACTOR CLAIMS THAT HE HEARD A RUMBLING INSIDE THE TANK, AND HE CLIMBED THE LADDER AND OPENED THE THIEF HATCH TO INVESTIGATE.  THE CONTRACTOR WAS BURNED AFTER HE OPENED THE THEIF HATCH AND WAS EXPOSED TO THE INTENSE HEAT BUILT UP FROM PROBABLE TANK FIRE.  THIS HEAT ESCAPED FROM THE HATCH AND CAUSED 1ST AND 2ND DEGREE BURNS ON HIS FACE AND LEFT HAND.  THE DRIVER WAS ADMITTED TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL FOR OBSERVANCE AND MEDICATED FOR PAIN.
narrative_clean: on tuesday night at approximately 9:00 pm, a driver for the water-hauling contractor (ems, inc) was burned by a field tank, while working at a kinder morgan storage facility locate in columbus jct, 1a (station 204). the contractor was draining on tank and while that tank was draining he attempted to use a propane torch to thaw a valve in preparation for draining another tank. the contractor had not hooked his drain hose to the second tank as it was being used at the other tank. a kinder morgan employee witnessed flames erupt from a 3" drain valve during the thawing process. the fire occurred as a result of the contractor opening the valve on the tank while using the torch. this allowed a path for an ignition source to enter the tank and also caused a small release of liquid which was ignited by the torch. failing to hook up the hose to the second tank before attempting to thaw the valve is against accepted practice. and opening up the valve while using the torch is a violation against the procedure set out in om 103 - hot work and against procedures reviewed in the kinder morgan contractor safety program. upon extinguishing the fire at the valve, the contractor claims that he heard a rumbling inside the tank, and he climbed the ladder and opened the thief hatch to investigate. the contractor was burned after he opened the theif hatch and was exposed to the intense heat built up from probable tank fire. this heat escaped from the hatch and caused 1st and 2nd degree burns on his face and left hand. the driver was admitted to a local hospital for observance and medicated for pain.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION CORP
NARRATIVE: A FLASH FIRE RESULTED IN SECOND DEGREE BURNS TO THE FACE OF MR. DAN WILLIAMS AND POLING AND BACON CONSTRUCTION COMPANY.  MR. WILLIAMS, WELDER'S HELPER, WAS HOLDING AND ALIGNING AN 8-INCH WELD END CAP TO AN EXISTING 20 X 8 INCH TEE.  WHEN THE CONTRACT WELDER STRUCK AN ARC TO BEGIN THE WELDING OPERATION, A FLASH FIRE OCCURRED. AN UNANTICIPATED COMBUSTIBLE GAS MIXTURE HAD DEVELOPED WITHIN THE NORTHERN END OF THE ABOVE GRADE LINE 1278 HEADER WITHIN THE EAGLE COMPRESSOR STATION YARD.  THIS COMBUSTIBLE MIXTURE WAS BELIEVED TO BE PRINCIPALLY ATTRIBUTED TO VALVE L-7208 LEAKING AND NOT BEING ABLE TO ACHIEVE ADEQUATE SHUT OFF AND THE REMOVAL OF THE PRIMARY FRESH AIR SOURCE.  ALIGNING THE WELD CAP OVER THE LAST SIGNIFICANT SOURCE OF FRESH AIR CHANGE THE FLOW DYNAMICS THAT HAD MAINTAINED NON-COMBUSTIBLE LIMITS JUST MOMENTS BEFORE.  TWO AIR MOVERS LOCATED AT BOTH ENDS OF THIS HEADER SYSTEM WERE EVACUATING THE PIPING AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT.  COLUMBIA WILL FILE A SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT WITH A MORE DETAILED ACCOUNT AND PHOTOGRAPHS. 12-11-03 THE INVESTIGATION RESTRICTED ITSELF TO THE EVENTS DIRECTLY CONNECTED TO THE SINGLE SUBJECT WELD ON THE SOUTHERN END OF THE LINE 1278 ABOVE GRADE HEADER. ON TUESDAY NIGHT, SEPTEMBER 9, 2003, COLUMBIA PERSONNEL BEGAN AN OVERSIGHT PROCESS TO BLOW DOWN LINE 1278 FROM SHELMIRE VALVE SETTING TO EAGLE COMPRESSOR STATION (A DISTANCE OF 4.26), THE 20-INCH LINE 1278 DISCHARGE HEADER INSIDE THE COMPRESSOR STATION FIRE VALVES, THE ABOVE GRADE LINE 1278 HEADER FEEDING NORTH, AND PARTS OF LINE 1556.  THE PURPOSE OF THIS BLOW DOWN WAS TO FACILITATE TIE-IN OF NEW LINE 1896 20-INCH PIPELINE AND MAKE MODIFICATIONS TO EXISTING PIPING.  SPECIFICALLY, THESE MODIFICATIONS CONSISTED OF THE REMOVAL OF EXISTING PIPING AND REGULATORS FABRICATED BETWEEN THE BLOW OFFS ON LINES 1278, 1804, AND 1896 AND THE SOUTHERN END OF THE LINE 1278 HEADER.  THESE BLOW OFFS ARE IMMEDIATELY WEST OF THE ABOVE GRADE LINE 1278 HEADER (SEE ATTAHCED PHOTOS) NIGHT WORK WAS UNDERTAKEN TO FACILITATE A SERIES OF OTHER CONSTRUCTION OUTAGES SCHEDULED FOR THE FOLLOWING DAY IN OTHER PARTS OF COLUMBIA'S PIPELINE SYSTEM.  AFTER THE INITIAL BLOW DOWN WAS COMPLETED AND AFTER OTHER TIE IN WORK WAS PERFORMED, A SMALL ONSITE CREW SET OUT TO WELD ON 8-INCH WELD END CAP IN A LOCATION WHERE PREVIOUS 10-INCH PIPING HAD BEEN CONNECTED WITH A 10 X 8 INCH REDUCER ON THE SOUTHERN END OF THE LINE 1278 HEADER SEE PHOTO P1 AND FIGURE 1.

NAME: ATLANTA GAS LIGHT CO
NARRATIVE: THIS EVENT IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION.  THERE HAS BEEN RECENTLY LOGGING AND UNAUTHORIZED GRADING WITHIN THE RIGHT-OF-WAY OF THIS PIPE.  ATLANTA GAS LIGHT COMPANY'S RIGHT-OF-WAY SURVEYOR, WHO HAD WALKED THIS LINE A WEEK BEFORE THE INCIDENT, REPORTED SIGNIFICANT LANDSCAPE AND GRADING CHANGES.  ATLANTA GAS LIGHT COMPANY WAS MADE AWARE OF THE PIPELINE FAILURE THROUGH MONITORING PRESSURE LOGS AT JESUP AND BELLE VISTA, DOWNSTREAM OF THE FAILURE. 6-28-04 ON SUNDAY, FEBRUARY 22, 2004 AT APPROXIMATELY 1:30 AM, A SECTION OF THE BRUNSWICK LATERAL 7.5 MILES SOUTH OF THE DOCTORTOWN (JESUP) MAINLINE VALVE (MLV) FAILED.  THE PRESSURE DROP WAS FIRST NOTED BY ATLANTA GAS LIGHT COMPANY PERSONNEL AT 1:35AM. THIS LINE IS LOCATED ON AN EASEMENT OWNED BY AGLC.  IN THE WEEK PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT, THE RIGHT-OF-WAY WAS INSPECTED BY AGLC PERSONNEL AND THE GRASS WAS MOWED.  AT THE TIME OF THAT INSPECTION, NO UNUSAL CONDITIONS WERE NOTED.  CONVERSELY, IN THE POST-INCIDENT INSPECTION THE FOLLOWING FACTS WERE MOTED: 1. HEAVY MACHINERY USED IN CONSTRUCTION AND GRADING ACTIVITIES WAS FOUND PARKED IN THE RIGHT-OF-WAY.  2. A DIRT PATH HAD BEEN ESTABLISHED ROUGHLY PERPENDICULAR TO THE PIPE ACROSS THE RIGHT-OF-WAY.  TIRE TRACKS WERE NOTED, INDICATING THAT THE HEAVY MACHINERY HAD CROSSED THE PIPE AT THIS LOCATION.  3.  A DRAINAGE CULVERT HAD BEEN INSTALLED ROUGHLY PERPENDICULAR TO AND UNDER THE PIPE ACROSS THE RIGHT-OF-WAY.  VISUAL INSPECTION OF THE RUPTURED PIPE AND FRAGMENTS FOUND ON-SITE SHOWED A GOUGE IN THE PIPE.  THE RUPTURE OCCURRED AT THE CULVERT WHERE THE SOIL WAS SATURATED.  SUBSEQUENT LABORATORY ANALYSIS INDICATED THAT THE GOUGE CONTAINED FRAGMENTS OF FOREIGN METALS, INDICATING DAMAGE BY A METALLIC OBJECT-MOST LIKELY THE HEAVY CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT SEEN ON-SITE.  IT WAS DETERMINED THAT EMBRITTLEMENT DUE TO HYDROGEN STRESS CRACKING OCCURRED AT THE SITE OF THE GOUGE.  THIS CRACKING WAS ACCELERATED DUE TO THE HIGH MOISTURE CONTENT OF THE SURROUNDING SOIL, AND ULTIMATELY LED TO THE FAILURE OF THE PIPE.

surveyor, who had walked this line a week before the incident, reported significant landscape and grading changes. atlanta gas light company was made aware of the pipeline failure through monitoring pressure logs at jesup and belle vista, downstream of the failure. 6-28-04 on sunday, february 22, 2004 at approximately 1:30 am, a section of the brunswick lateral 7.5 miles south of the doctortown (jesup) mainline valve (mlv) failed. the pressure drop was first noted by atlanta gas light company personnel at 1:35am. this line is located on an easement owned by aglc. in the week prior to the incident, the right-of-way was inspected by aglc personnel and the grass was mowed. at the time of that inspection, no unusal conditions were noted. conversely, in the post-incident inspection the following facts were moted: 1. heavy machinery used in construction and grading activities was found parked in the right-of-way. 2. a dirt path had been established roughly perpendicular to the pipe across the right-of-way. tire tracks were noted, indicating that the heavy machinery had crossed the pipe at this location. 3. a drainage culvert had been installed roughly perpendicular to and under the pipe across the right-of-way. visual inspection of the ruptured pipe and fragments found on-site showed a gouge in the pipe. the rupture occurred at the culvert where the soil was saturated. subsequent laboratory analysis indicated that the gouge contained fragments of foreign metals, indicating damage by a metallic object-most likely the heavy construction equipment seen on-site. it was determined that embrittlement due to hydrogen stress cracking occurred at the site of the gouge. this cracking was accelerated due to the high moisture content of the surrounding soil, and ultimately led to the failure of the pipe.

NAME: TEXAS GAS TRANSMISSION LLC
NARRATIVE: ON THE EVENING OF DECEMBER 24, 2004 AT 10:30 PM (CST) TEXAS GAS' GAS CONTROL DEPT RECEIVED NOTIFICATION FROM A GAUGER.  MR. GENE GILES [PHONE NO (985)232-9830], WITH HILCORP ENGINEERING THAT OUR TEXACO-DOG LAKE (METER NO 9836) FACILITIES WERE ON FIRE.  THIS METER FACILITY IS ON A SMALL CONCRETE PLATFORM IN THE LOUISIANA MARSH.  HILCORP ENGINEERING OPERATES PRODUCTION IN THE DOG LAKE AREA.  TEXAS GAS WAS RECEIVING APPROXIMATELY 17 MMCF/D RATE AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT.      THE INCIDENT WAS REPORTED TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER BY 12:30 A.M. (CST) DECEMBER 25TH.  AFTER THE INITIAL CALL FROM MR. GILES, GAS CONTROL IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIED THE YOUNGSVILLE-MORGAN CITY DISTRICT ONE-CALL PERSON WHO MOBILIZED WITH THREE EMPLOYEES FROM THE MORGAN CITY DISTRICT WHO ARRIVED BY CONTRACTED CREW BOAT AT THE AREA OF THE PLATFORM BY 1:30 A.M. AND FOUND THAT OUR PLATFORM WAS NOT ON FIRE, BUT PIPING 10- TO 15- FEET FROM THE PLATFORM WAS.  THEY PROCEEDED TO ISOLATE THE TEXAS GAS PIPING DOWNSTREAM OF THE AFFECTED FACILITIES.  HILCORP THEN SHUT IN THEIR PRODUCTION AND THERE WERE NO ACTIVE METERS UPSTREAM.  SINCE TRANSCO HAS AN "INACTIVE" RISER AND SIDE VALVE INTERCONNECT (NO 8122) ON THE PLATFORM, WE NOTIFIED THEIR GAS CONTROL DEPT PROMPTLY.      AFTER OUR PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED, THE FIRE CONTINUED AT THE SAME RATE.  OUR EMPLOYEES REPORTED THAT THE FIRE APPEARED TO BE ORIGINATING FROM THE TRANSCO PIPELINE AREA.  WE REPORTED THIS TO TRANSCO WHO THEN BEGAN MOBILIZING THEIR EMPLOYEES WHO ARRIVED ONSITE THE MORNING OF DECEMBER 25.  THEY ISOLATED BOTH THEIR 6-INCH GAS PIPELINE AND A 3-INCH LIQUIDS PIPELINE WITH NO IMPACT TO THE FLAME.      AT APPROXIMATELY 10:00 A.M.  DECEMBER 25, AS REPORTED TO US BY A HILCORP ENGINEERING REPRESENTATIVE, THE FLAME GREATLY INTENSIFIED.  TEXAS GAS BELIEVES THAT THIS GREATLY INTENSIFIED FLAME INDICATES THE RUPTURE OF OUR CBD 8" PIPELINE IN THE RISER LEAVING THE PLATFORM, DUE TO THE HEAT FROM THE FIRE.  AT ABOUT THIS TIME, 10:00 A.M. DECEMBER 25, 2004, HILCORP ENGINEERING BEGAN MANUALLY SHUTTING-IN THEIR PRODUCTION LINES.  THE FIRE DIMINISHED AND SUBSIDED OVER THE NEXT 2 TO 3 HOURS.  WE HAD NO EMPLOYEES AT THE SITE WHEN THIS EVENT OCCURRED AS WE WERE IN THE PROCESS OF CHANGING CREWS AND REFUELING THE BOAT.  THIS INFORMATIONS WAS RELAYED FROM THE HILCORP CREW BOAT THAT WAS ALSO MONITORING THE SITUATION.      TEXAS GAS BELIEVES THAT THE INITIAL FIRE WAS CAUSED BY THE FAILURE AND IGNITION OF A PRODUCTION LINE OWNED BY HILCORP ENGINEERING.  THE HEAT FORM THIS INITIAL FIRE CAUSED TEXAS GAS' CBD 8" PIPELINE TO RUPTURE.    HILCORP REIMBURSED TEXAS GAS FOR THE MAJORITY OF THE LOSS.  TEXAS GAS REPAIRED THE FACILITY ON PROJECT 46867.

NAME: QUESTAR GAS COMPANY
NARRATIVE: THIS PIPE RUPTURED AT OR NEAR THE SITE WHERE A CORROSION PIT HAD BEEN REPAIRED BY FILLING WITH WELD MATERIAL.  CONSTRUCTION RECORDS INDICATE THAT THIS REPAIR WAS MADE PRIOR TO INSTALLING THE PIPE IN 1955.  A METALLURGICAL INVESTIGATION BY EWI WORKING IN CONJUNCTION WITH AMERICAN METALLURGICAL SERVICES CONCLUDED THAT "THE FEEDER-LINE 18 FAILURE ORIGIN WAS IN A WELD REGION NEAR THE BOTTOM OF THE PIPELINE."  THE INVESTIGATION FOUND NO EVIDENCE OF ACTIVE CORROSION, FATIGUE CRACKING, HYDROGEN STRESS CRACKING, OR STRESS CORROSION CRACKING.    FURTHER, THE METALLURGICAL INVESTIGATION FOUND THAT "THE ORIENTATION OF THE FRACTURE AND THE DISTINCT DOG-LEG APPEARANCE OF THE REMOVED PIPELINE SECTION WOULD SUGGEST AN EXTERNAL LOAD MAY HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE FRACTURE."  AN INVESTIGATION OF POTENTIAL EXTERNAL LOADING DID FIND THAT ADDITIONAL THIRD-PARTY FILL HAD BEEN PLACED OVER THE PIPELINE IN THE REGION OF THE FRACTURE, AND THAT OTHER UTILITIES HAD BEEN INSTALLED UNDER THE PIPELINE IN THIS SAME AREA.  HOWEVER, IT COULD NOT BE CONCLUDED THAT THESE FACTORS OR OTHER FACTORS INCLUDING NATURALLY OCCURRING OUTSIDE FORCES ALONE PROVIDED SUFFICIENT EXTERNAL LOADING TO HAVE CAUSED THIS FAILURE.
narrative_clean: this pipe ruptured at or near the site where a corrosion pit had been repaired by filling with weld material. construction records indicate that this repair was made prior to installing the pipe in 1955. a metallurgical investigation by ewi working in conjunction with american metallurgical services concluded that "the feeder-line 18 failure origin was in a weld region near the bottom of the pipeline." the investigation found no evidence of active corrosion, fatigue cracking, hydrogen stress cracking, or stress corrosion cracking. further, the metallurgical investigation found that "the orientation of the fracture and the distinct dog-leg appearance of the removed pipeline section would suggest an external load may have contributed to the fracture." an investigation of potential external loading did find that additional third-party fill had been placed over the pipeline in the region of the fracture, and that other utilities had been installed under the pipeline in this same area. however, it could not be concluded that these factors or other factors including naturally occurring outside forces alone provided sufficient external loading to have caused this failure.

NARRATIVE: ON SUNDAY APRIL 9, A FIRE WAS OBSERVED AT DELMONT COMPRESSOR STATION. THE FIRE WAS CONFINED TO A SINGLE COMPRESSOR UNTI. TRANSITE BUILDING SIDING WAS DAMAGED, POTENTIALLY RELEASING ASBESTOS INTO THE BUILDING. THE FIRE WAS QUARANTINED DUE TO THE CONCERN OF EMPLOYEE EXPOSURE TO ASBESTOS. AN AIR MONITORING CONTRACTOR WAS BROUGHT IN AND VERIFIED NO ASBESTOS HAD BEEN RELEASED AND THE QUARANTINE WAS LIFTED ON THURSDAY APRIL 13, ALLOWING A MORE THOROUGH INVESTIGATION TO PROCEED AFTER THE EASTER HOLIDAY. THE GAS VENTED FROM THE CRANKCASE INTO THE COMPRESSOR BUILDING AND IGNITED WHICH APPEARS TO HAVE CAUSED THE DAMAGE TO THE OIL SYSTEM. NAME: ENTERPRISE PRODUCTS OPERATING L.P.
NARRATIVE: LEAK WAS REPORTED ON OUR WEBB COUNTY 20" PIPELINE ON NOVEMBER 25, 2006.  THE LEAK WAS AT THE LOCATION OF A NEW HOT TAP INSTALLATION WE HAD MADE ON THIS PIPELINE EARLIER IN 2006 AND THE LEAK RATE WAS MINIMAL.  AFTER INITIAL REVIEW, A DECISION WAS MADE TO TAKE THE PIPELINE OUT OF SERVICE SO IT COULD BE FURTHER EVALUATED.  THIS ACTION WAS THE INITIAL ACTION THAT MADE THE INCIDENT REPORTABLE TO THE RAILROAD COMMISSION OF TEXAS.  THE NOTIFICATION TO THE STATE OCCURED WITHIN TWO HOURS OF THAT DECISION AND WAS MADE ON NOVEMBER 25, 2006 BY DOUG MENKE, OPERATIONS SUPERVISOR.  OUR INITIAL ASSUMPTION WAS PROVEN TO BE CORRECT IN THAT WE CONFIRMED THAT WE HAD A LEAKING HOT TAP CLAMP.  THE CLAMP VENDOR TRAVELLED TO THE LOCATION TO INJECT SEALANT IN THE HOT TAP FITTING TO TRY AND STOP THE LEAK.  IT WAS CONFIRMED AT THAT TIME THAT THE PIPE WAS ALSO LEAKING AND THAT A REPAIR OF A LEAKING SEAL WOULD NOT HANDLE THE REPAIR.  A DECISION WAS MADE THAT WE WOULD HAVE TO CUT OUT PIPE AND REPLACE THE HOT TAP ASSEMBLY AND LEAKING PIPE.  THIS DECISION CAUSED THE REPAIR COST ESTIMATE TO NOW EXCEED THE $50,000 REPORTING THRESHOLD.  OPERATIONS NOTIFED COMPLIANCE OF THIS DECISION VIA AN EMAIL ON THE MORNING OF DECEMBER 11, 2006.  BASED ON THIS NEW INFORMATION NOTIFICATION OF THIS BEING A REPORTABLE INCIDENT WAS MADE TO THE NRC.  THE FITTING ASSEMBLY AND PIPE WERE SENT TO A METALLURGIST FOR EXAMINATION.  THE METALLUGICAL ANALYSIS REPORTED THAT ONE OF THE SEALS ON THE HOT TAP CLAMP DID NOT SEAT PROPERLY AND OVER A PERIOD OF TIME BEGAN TO LEAK GAS INTO THE CAVITY BETWEEN THE PRIMARY AND SECONDARY SEAL.  IN TIME, THE SECONDARY SEAL FAILED AND GAS BEGAN JETTING TOWARD THE BODY OF THE PIPE UNTIL SUCH TIME THAT THE MAIN 20" PIPELINE WAS CUT AND STARTED TO LEAK.  THE VENDOR REPORTED THAT THIS WAS THE FIRST FAILURE OF ITS TYPE ON THIS TYPE OF HOT TAP CLAMP INSTALLATION AND IS TAKING ACTIONS TO IMPROVE THEIR SEAL DESIGN. THE PIPELINE WAS PLACED BACK INTO SERVICE AFTER A TEE WAS WELDED INTO THE PIPELINE ELIMINATING THE NEED FOR A BOLT ON CLAMP AT THIS TIE IN CONNECTION.
narrative_clean: leak was reported on our webb county 20" pipeline on november 25, 2006. the leak was at the location of a new hot tap installation we had made on this pipeline earlier in 2006 and the leak rate was minimal. after initial review, a decision was made to take the pipeline out of service so it could be further evaluated. this action was the initial action that made the incident reportable to the railroad commission of texas. the notification to the state occured within two hours of that decision and was made on november 25, 2006 by doug menke, operations supervisor. our initial assumption was proven to be correct in that we confirmed that we had a leaking hot tap clamp. the clamp vendor travelled to the location to inject sealant in the hot tap fitting to try and stop the leak. it was confirmed at that time that the pipe was also leaking and that a repair of a leaking seal would not handle the repair. a decision was made that we would have to cut out pipe and replace the hot tap assembly and leaking pipe. this decision caused the repair cost estimate to now exceed the $50,000 reporting threshold. operations notifed compliance of this decision via an email on the morning of december 11, 2006. based on this new information notification of this being a reportable incident was made to the nrc. the fitting assembly and pipe were sent to a metallurgist for secondary seal. in time, the secondary seal failed and gas began jetting toward the body of the pipe until such time that the main 20" pipeline was cut and started to leak. the vendor reported that NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON AUGUST 10, 2007 NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPLETED NSTALLATION OF A 24-INCH PIGABLE BYPASS PIPING TO FACILITATE REMOVAL OF LATERAL LINES TO THE NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPRESSION PLATFORM MI 686 C-CMP. ALL WORK WAS COMPLETED AND THE PIPING WAS RE-PRESSURIZED AND LEAK TESTED. LATE THAT DAY PERSONNEL IN AIRCRAFT WITNESSED BUBBLES ON THE OCEAN SURFACE IN THE WORK AREA THAT WERE INDICATIVE OF A GAS LEAK FROM THE PIPING. PRODUCER PLATFORMS WERE NOTIFIED TO SHUT-IN AND THE LINE WAS ISOLATED. THIS WAS REPORTED TO MMS AND THE COAST GUARD. PRESSURE WAS REDUCED ON THE LINE. A REPAIR PLAN WAS SUBMITTED TO & APPROVED BY MMS. INVESTIGATION FOUND THAT THERE WAS A SMALL CRACK ON A 2-INCH BYPASS LINE THAT WENT AROUND A 24-INCH SUB SEA BLOCK VALVE. WHILE WORKING ON REPAIRING THIS LEAK BY REMOVING THE 2 INCH CONNECTION PIPING TO THE 24-INCH LINE AS WELL AS THE SADDLE TO FACILITATE INSTALLATION OF A 24-INCH LEAK CLAMP, IT WAS FOUND THAT THE 2-INCH CONNECTION ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE BLOCK VALVE WAS ALSO CRACKED. A REVISED REPAIR PLAN WAS SUBMITTED AND APPROVED BY MMS. THE REVISED PLAN CALLED FOR REMOVAL OF THE TWO INCH PIPE AND SADDLE IDENTICAL TO WHAT WAS COMPLETED ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE VALVE AND INSTALLATION OF A HIGH PRESSURE, FULL ENCIRCLEMENT, BOLT-ON LEAK CLAMP. BOTH LEAK CLAMPS WERE INSTALLED AND A LEAK TEST AT NORMAL OPERATING PRESSURE WAS CONDUCTED FOR 2 HOURS. THERE WERE NO LEAKS OBSERVED AND THE PIPING WAS WRAPPED AND SANDBAGGED TO ORIGINAL COVER. THIS WAS COMPLETED ON AUGUST 31, 2007. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE LEAKS IS STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION AS IT IS THOUGHT THAT THE CONTRACTOR CRACKED THE PIPE WHEN INSTALLING SANDBAGS AFTER THE 24 INCH BYPASS LINE INSTALLATION WAS COMPLETE. A METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS IS BEING CONDUCTED ON THE 2-INCH REMOVED PIPING. A SUPPLEMENTAL/FINAL REPORT IS BEING FILED WITH UPDATE TO THE COST OF GAS LOSS AND REPAIRS.
narrative_clean: on august 10, 2007 northern natural gas completed nstallation of a 24-inch pigable bypass piping to facilitate removal of lateral lines to the northern natural gas compression platform mi 686 c-cmp. all work was completed and the piping was re-pressurized and leak tested. late that day personnel in aircraft witnessed bubbles on the ocean surface in the work area that were indicative of a gas leak from the piping. producer platforms were notified to shut-in and the line was isolated. this was reported to mms and the coast guard. pressure was reduced on the line. a repair plan was submitted to & approved by mms. investigation found that there was a small crack on a 2-inch bypass line that went around a 24-inch sub sea block valve. while working on repairing this leak by removing the 2 inch connection piping to the 24-inch line as well as the saddle to facilitate installation of a 24-inch leak clamp, it was found that the 2-inch connection on the other side of the block valve was also cracked. a revised repair plan was submitted and approved by mms. the revised plan called for removal of the two inch pipe and saddle identical to what was completed on the other side of the valve and installation of a high pressure, full encirclement, bolt-on leak clamp. both leak clamps were installed and a leak test at normal operating pressure was conducted for 2 hours. there were no leaks observed and the piping was wrapped and sandbagged to original cover. this was completed on august 31, 2007. the root cause of the leaks is still under investigation as it is thought that the contractor cracked the pipe when installing sandbags after the 24 inch bypass line installation was complete. a metallurgical analysis is being conducted on the 2-inch removed piping. a supplemental/final report is being filed with update to the cost of gas loss and repairs.

UPON ISOLATION AND BLOWDOWN OF THE VALVE SECTION, THE LINE WAS EXCAVATED AND A CRACK IN THE CIRCUMFERENTIAL WELD OR WELD AREA WAS FOUND TO BE THE SOURCE OF THE LEAKING GAS.  METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS REVEALED POORLY COMPLETED WELDING DURING THE ORIGINAL CONSTRUCTION THAT FAILED DUE TO TENSILE STRESSES ALONG THE PIPE IN A LONGITUDINAL DIRECTION.  FURTHER INVESTIGATION SHOWED THAT THE BACKFILL SURROUNDING THE PIPELINE HAD BEEN DISTURBED FOR CONSTRUCTION ON A PARALLEL PIPELINE.  THE FAILED PIPELINE MAY NOT HAVE BEEN ADEQUATELY SUPPORTED BEFORE ITS COVER WAS RESTORED, RESULTING IN THE EXTRA TENSILE STRESSES.  ABOUT 80 FEET OF PIPE WAS REMOVED AND REPLACED WITH NEW PIPE.  THE PIPELINE SEGMENT IS BACK IN SERVICE.
narrative_clean: a third party noticed hole in ground and hissing sound in the vicinity of southern natural gas (sng) company's 18" south main pipeline. he reported this to sng and company personnel were dispatched to the site. upon isolation and blowdown of the valve section, the line was excavated and a crack in the circumferential weld or weld area was found to be the source of the leaking gas. metallurgical analysis revealed poorly completed welding during the original construction that failed due to tensile stresses along the pipe in a longitudinal direction. further investigation showed that the backfill surrounding the pipeline had been disturbed for construction on a parallel pipeline. the failed pipeline may not have been adequately supported before its cover was restored, resulting in the extra tensile stresses. about 80 feet of pipe was removed and replaced with new pipe. the pipeline segment is back in service.

NAME: MISSISSIPPI RIVER TRANSMISSION CORP
NARRATIVE: DURING A STORM, A TRANSFORMER STATION AT THE MAGENSIUM ELEKTRON PLANT WHICH WAS ABOUT 100 YARDS FROM OUR METER STATION ,OFF OF LINE A-102, WAS STRUCK BY LIGHTNING CAUSING THE SECONDARY SIDE OF THE TRANSFORMER STATION TO EXPLODE. APPARENTLY THE SPARKS OR DEBRIS FELL OR WAS BLOWN INSIDE THE METER BUILDING AND LANDED ON THE PRESSURE CONTROLLER FOR THE REGULATOR. THIS RESULTED IN A FIRE FROM LEAKAGE AROUND THE DOOR OF THE CONTROLLER. AS A RESULT OF THE HEAT FROM THE FIRE, THE BOURDON TUBE IN THE PRESSURE CONTROLLER WAS DAMAGED CAUSING THE REGULATOR TO OPEN UP AND THEN THE RELIEF VALVE STARTED BLOWING. THE FIRE WAS CONTAINED TO THE CONTROLLER AND A LITTLE SURFACE DAMAGE TO THE ACTUATOR OF THE REGULATOR.  WHILE THIS EVENT DID NOT MEET THE CRITERIA OF AN INCIDENT IN §191.3,PARAGRAPHS (1) OR (2), IT WAS DEEMED SIGNIFICANT IN THE JUDGMENT OF THE OPERATOR BECAUSE OF THE FIRE.
narrative_clean: during a storm, a transformer station at the magensium elektron plant which was about 100 yards from our meter station ,off of line a-102, was struck by lightning causing the secondary side of the transformer station to explode. apparently the sparks or debris fell or was blown inside the meter building and landed on the pressure controller for the regulator. this resulted in a fire from leakage around the door of the controller. as a result of the heat from the fire, the bourdon tube in the pressure controller was damaged causing the regulator to open up and then the relief valve started blowing. the fire was contained to the controller and a little surface damage to the actuator of the regulator. while this event did not meet the criteria of an incident in §191.3,paragraphs (1) or (2), it was deemed significant in the judgment of the operator because of the fire.

NAME: PRAXAIR, INC
NARRATIVE: VALERO REFINERY, TEXAS CITY CALLED AT ~22:40 TO REPORT A HYDROGEN LEAK FROM PRAXAIR'S SYSTEM IN THE VICINITY OF THEIR ADMIN. BUILDING.  FOLLOW-UP COMMUNICATIONS INDICATED THE LEAK INVOLVED A FIRE AS WELL, WHICH SEEMED TO CONFIRM THE POTENTIAL FOR A REAL HYDROGEN LEAK.  VALERO REFINERY CONTACTED LOCAL EMERGENCY RESPONDERS (TEXAS CITY PD AND FD) WHO CAME TO THE SITE.    FIVE OF PRAXAIR'S PERSONNEL WERE DISPATCHED TO THE SITE, INCLUDING THE PIPELINE MANAGER AND PIPELINE SUPERINTENDENT WHO WAS FIRST ON THE SCENE).  THE PRAXAIR PERSONNEL DID NOT SEE ANY FIRE, BUT COULD HEAR LEAKING GAS FROM THE VICINITY OF THE HIGH-PRESSURE H2 METER STATION/LETDOWN STATION (THERE ARE ALSO N2 AND O2 PIPELINES IN THE VICINITY AS WELL AS AN O2 METER STATION).  NEITHER THE HIGH-PRESSURE H2 METER STATION, NOR THE LETDOWN STATION WERE IN ACTIVE USE AT THE TIME (IN FACT, THE METER STATION WAS ISOLATED DOWNSTREAM AT THE PSA INSIDE THE VALERO REFINERY).  THE EMERGENCY RESPONDERS BLOCKED OFF LOOP 197 IN FRONT OF THE REFINERY AND MADE PREPARATIONS TO PUT WATER ON THE STATION IN CASE OF AN ENERGY RELEASE AS INSTRUCTED BY PX PERSONNEL.    AT 00:30, ALL PX PERSONNEL WERE ON-SITE.  THE TEXAS CITY FD WAS PUTTING WATER ON THE STATION.  A PLAN WAS FORMULATED TO SEND TWO 2-MAN TEAMS TO INVESTIGATE AND ISOLATE THE LEAK.  MULTI-USE ANALYZERS AND RAGS FASTENED TO THE END OF PROBING BARS WOULD BE USED TO INDENTIFY THE PRESENCE OF A LEAK AND/OR BURNING H2.  THE TEAMS WOULD UNLOCK, OPEN, AND ENTER THROUGH DIFFERENT GATES.  PRIOR TO ENTRY, 110V POWER WAS ISOLATED FROM THE STATION.  THE PLAN WAS COMMUNICATED TO PRAXAIR OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT, THE PIPELINE CONTROL CENTER, AND PERSONNEL ON-SITE.  HWP WAS ISSUED.  UPON ENTERING THE GATE, THE TEAM ENTERING THE NORTH GATE NOTED THAT THE LEAK WAS COMING FROM A KUNKLE PRV ON THE INSTRUMENT (N2) GAS PANEL.  THE PRV WAS MANUALLY CLOSED AND THE STATION WAS SNIFFED FOR ANY H2 LEAKS.  NONE WERE FOUND.  110V POWER WAS RESTORED TO THE STATION.    THE FINDINGS WERE COMMUNICATED TO THE VALERO REFINERY AND THE EMERGENCY RESPONDERS, AND THE EMERGENCY WAS CLOSED AT 01:05.  INVESTIGATION INTO THE CAUSE OF THE LIFTING OF THE PRV IS ONGOING.
narrative_clean: valero refinery, texas city called at ~22:40 to report a hydrogen leak from praxair's system in the vicinity of their admin. building. follow-up communications indicated the leak involved a fire as well, which seemed to confirm the potential for a real hydrogen leak. valero refinery contacted local emergency responders (texas city pd and fd) who came to the site. five of praxair's personnel were dispatched to the site, including the pipeline manager and pipeline superintendent who was first on the scene). the praxair personnel did not see any fire, but could hear leaking gas from the vicinity of the high-pressure h2 meter station/letdown station (there are also n2 and o2 pipelines in the vicinity as well as an o2 meter station). neither the high-pressure h2 meter station, nor the letdown station were in active use at the time (in fact, the meter station was isolated downstream at the psa inside the valero refinery). the emergency responders blocked off loop 197 in front of the refinery and made preparations to put water on the station in case of an energy release as instructed by px personnel. at 00:30, all px personnel were on-site. the texas city fd was putting water on the station. a plan was formulated to send two 2-man teams to investigate and isolate the leak. multi-use analyzers and rags fastened to the end of probing bars would be used to indentify the presence of a leak and/or burning h2. the teams would unlock, open, and enter through different gates. prior to entry, 110v power was isolated from the station. the plan was communicated to praxair operations management, the pipeline control center, and personnel on-site. hwp was issued. upon entering the gate, the team entering the north gate noted that the leak was coming from a kunkle prv on the instrument (n2) gas panel. the prv was manually closed and the station was sniffed for any h2 leaks. none were found. 110v power was restored to the station. the findings were communicated to the valero refinery and the emergency responders, and the emergency was closed at 01:05. investigation into the cause of the lifting of the prv is ongoing.

NAME: STONE ENERGY
NARRATIVE: ON JUNE 30, 2008 WE RECEIVED A REPORT FROM MINERALS MANAGEMENT SERVICE OUT OF LAKE CHARLES LOUISIANA. MMS REPORTED THAT DURING A FLY BY OF THE WEST CAMERON FIELD NEAR THE WC45 PLATFORM, AN OIL SHEEN WAS REPORTED TO BE FLOATING IN THE FIELD AND BUBBLES COMING UP TO THE SURFACE FROM WHAT APPEARED TO BE A LEAKING PIPELINE.   STONE ENERGY CORPORATION TOOK IMMEDIATE ACTION TO HAVE THE ONLY PIPELINE IN THE AREA AT WC45 SHUT IN, AND WE ACTIVATED THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE TEAM. WE CONDUCTED AN IMMEDIATE FLY BY FROM THE WC45 FACILITY TO THE BEACH FACILITY AT JOHNSON BAYOU. STONE ENERGY CORPORATION WAS TRANSPORTING HYDROCARBONS TO THE BEACH IN A 16¿ PIPELINE WHICH IS REGISTERED AS A DOT LINE.   STONE ENERGY CORPORATION DISPATCHED A JACK- UP BOAT, DIVE BOAT WITH DIVERS, AND SENT A FIELD BOAT INTO THE AREA TO WARN MARINERS OF THE POSSIBLE HAZARD. AT THIS TIME IT WAS STILL UNDETERMINED THAT THE LEAK WAS COMING FROM OUR PIPELINE, ACTIVATION OF A SKIMMER UNIT TO ENSURE THAT NO HYDROCARBONS WOULD REACH THE BEACH IF THE LEAK BECAME WORST. WHEN ARRIVING ON LOCATION WE JUMPED THE DIVERS AND THEY LOCATED A SMALL CRACK IN THE PROTECTIVE CONCRETE COVERING ON THE PIPELINE, THEY COULD NOT FIND THE LEAK WITH OUT REMOVING THE COVERING. DIVERS MECHANICALLY REMOVED THE COVERING AND LOCATED A SMALL PINHOLE LOCATED AT THE 6 O CLOCK POSITION. AREA WAS PREPARED FOR A SPLIT CLAMP REPAIR KIT AND DIVERS INSTALLED IT ON THE PIPELINE AND SEALED THE LEAKING AREA.   STONE ENERGY CORPORATION HAS CHOSEN TO REMOVE THE 16¿ PIPELINE FROM SERVICE, THE LINE HAS BEEN FLUSHED AND PICKLED AND IS PREPARED FOR REMOVAL AT THE BEACH AREA. AT THIS TIME WE HAVE NO FURTHER INFORMATION ON THE DOT LINE.
narrative_clean: on june 30, 2008 we received a report from minerals management service out of lake charles louisiana. mms reported that during a fly by of the west cameron field near the wc45 platform, an oil sheen was reported to be floating in the field and bubbles coming up to the surface from what appeared to be a leaking pipeline. stone energy corporation took immediate action to have the only pipeline in the area at wc45 shut in, and we activated the emergency response team. we conducted an immediate fly by from the wc45 facility to the beach facility at johnson bayou. stone energy corporation was transporting hydrocarbons to the beach in a 16¿ pipeline which is registered as a dot line. stone energy corporation dispatched a jack- up boat, dive boat with divers, and sent a field boat into the area to warn mariners of the possible hazard. at this time it was still undetermined that the leak was coming from our pipeline, activation of a skimmer unit to ensure that no hydrocarbons would reach the beach if the leak became worst. when arriving on location we jumped the divers and they located a small crack in the protective concrete covering on the pipeline, they could not find the leak with out removing the covering. divers mechanically removed the covering and located a small pinhole located at the 6 o clock position. area was prepared for a split clamp repair kit and divers installed it on the pipeline and sealed the leaking area. stone energy corporation has chosen to remove the 16¿ pipeline from service, the line has been flushed and pickled and is prepared for removal at the beach area. at this time we have no further information on the dot line.

NAME: DOMINION TRANSMISSION, INC
NARRATIVE: WHILE RECLAIMING SPOIL, DURING THE CONSTRUCTION OF TL-532, THAT WAS STORED OFF TO THE SIDE OF TL-522 ON A SLOPE BETWEEN THE FENCE FOR THE DOMINION COVE POINT LNG FACILITY AND RECEIVING PIT FOR GRAY'S CREEK BORE, A BULLDOZER WAS BELIEVED TO HAVE HIT 36" TL-522 AS GAS BEGAN TO BLOW FROM THE PIPE.   ALL EQUIPMENT WAS SHUT OFF AND EMPLOYEES EVACUATED THE AREA AT AROUND 9:30 AM.  DOMINION TRANSMISSION INC. (DTI) MANAGEMENT IN CLARKSBURG WAS CONTACTED ABOUT THE ACCIDENT AND BEGAN KEEPING CONSTANT CONTACT WITH STAFF AT COVE POINT BY PHONE UNTIL GARY BAKER; DTI¿S CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISOR ARRIVED ON SITE.  AFTER LOWERING THE PRESSURE TO GET A BETTER LOOK AT THE DAMAGED AREA IT WAS DETERMINED THAT A ONE-INCH TAP WAS BROKEN OFF OF TL-522, AS YOU COULD SEE A ONE-INCH HOLE IN THE PIPE. LYING OFF TO THE SIDE WAS A SHORT PIECE OF ONE-INCH PIPE, A ONE-INCH VALVE, AND THEN ANOTHER PIECE OF ONE-INCH PIPE SEVERAL FEET LONG WITH PART STILL COVERED BY DIRT.  BASED ON RECORDS FROM WHEN COLUMBIA GAS OWNED THE PIPELINE 30 YEARS AGO, DTI DETERMINED THAT COLUMBIA PUT THE TAP ON THE PIPELINE AS PART OF A LEAK DETECTION SYSTEM THAT WAS ONLY UTILIZED FOR A SHORT TIME.      THE PIPELINE SECTION TO WHICH THE ONE-INCH TAP WAS CONNECTED IS APPROXIMATELY 7 MILES IN LENGTH AND ONLY ONE CUSTOMER TAP WAS CONNECTED IN THIS SECTION BEING A FEED TO WASHINGTON GAS & LIGHT (WGL) CALLED THE PATUXENT METER STATION.  BY REDUCING THE PRESSURE FROM 910 PSIG TO 350 PSIG, DTI WAS ABLE TO KEEP FEEDING THE PATUXENT METER STATION TO KEEP WGL IN SERVICE.  AFTER SEVERAL CONFERENCE CALLS ON HOW TO REPAIR THE BROKEN TAP AND STILL MAINTAIN 100% SERVICE TO WGL AT PATUXENT, DTI DECIDED TO CONTRACT IN LNG TANK TRUCKS TO FEED WGL WHILE THE TL-522 LINE WAS BLOWN DOWN AND THE BROKEN TAP REPAIRED. DTI FINISHED REPAIRING THE TAP AND PLACED TL-522 BACK IN SERVICE AT 6:30 A.M., ON SUNDAY MORNING THE 16TH OF NOVEMBER.  NO SERVICE INTERRUPTIONS WERE EXPERIENCED BY WGL OR ITS CUSTOMERS BECAUSE OF THE LNG USED TO KEEP WGL¿S SYSTEM WHOLE.
narrative_clean: while reclaiming spoil, during the construction of tl-532, that was stored off to the side of tl-522 on a slope between the fence for the dominion cove point lng facility and receiving pit for gray's creek bore, a bulldozer was believed to have hit 36" tl-522 as gas began to blow from the pipe. all equipment was shut off and employees evacuated the area at around 9:30 am. dominion transmission inc. (dti) management in clarksburg was contacted about the accident and began keeping constant contact with staff at cove point by phone until gary baker; dti¿s construction supervisor arrived on site. after lowering the pressure to get a better look at the damaged area it was determined that a one-inch tap was broken off of tl-522, as you could see a one-inch hole in the pipe. lying off to the side was a short piece of one-inch pipe, a one-inch valve, and then another piece of one-inch pipe several feet long with part still covered by dirt. based on records from when columbia gas owned the pipeline 30 years ago, dti determined that columbia put the tap on the pipeline as part of a leak detection system that was only utilized for a short time. the pipeline section to which the one-inch tap was connected is approximately 7 miles in length and only one customer tap was connected in this section being a feed to washington gas & light (wgl) called the patuxent meter station. by reducing the pressure from 910 psig to 350 psig, dti was able to keep feeding the patuxent meter station to keep wgl in service. after several conference calls on how to repair the broken tap and still maintain 100% service to wgl at patuxent, dti decided to contract in lng tank trucks to feed wgl while the tl-522 line was blown down and the broken tap repaired. dti finished repairing the tap and placed tl-522 back in service at 6:30 a.m., on sunday morning the 16th of november. no service interruptions were experienced by wgl or its customers because of the lng used to keep wgl¿s system whole.

NAME: DOMINION EAST OHIO

PRELIMINARY DAMAGE ASSESSMENT INDICATED DAMAGE TO THE #4 COMPRESSOR UNIT AIR INTAKE, SCAVENGING UNITL LOWER CONVERS ON #4 AND #5 COMPRESSOR CYLINDERS AND THE TURBO-CHARGER. AN INVESTIGATION WS CONDUCTED BY DOMINION EAST OHIO AND THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF OHIO ON SEPTEMBER 27, 2006 AT APPROXIMATELY 3:00 PM TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER AND TO THE PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION OF OHIO BY TELEPHONE. FURTHER INVESTIGATION REVEALED THAT THE #4 COMPRESSOR UNIT HAD SHUT DOWN ON SEPTEMBER 26, 2006 AT APPROXIMATELY 6:58 PM DUE TO AN OVER-SPEED CONDITION.  THE COMPRESSOR OPERATOR ATTEMPTED TO RE-START THE UNIT, THE UNIT BACKFIRED.  THE COMPRESSOR OOPERATOR SUSPECTED FUEL IN THE AIR INTAKE, PURGED THE INTAKE WITH AIR AND RE-STARTED THE UNIT.  JACKSON TOWNSHIP FIRE DEPARTMENT RESPONDED TO AN EXPLOSION CALL FROM A LOCAL RESIDENT AT APPROXIMATELY 7:30 PM.  FIRE DEPARTMENT PERSONNEL SPOKE WITH THE COMPRESSOR OPERATOR AND DETERMINED THE RESIDENT HAD HEARD THE BACK-FIRE OF #4 COMPRESSOR UNIT.  ALL FOUR COMPRESSORS OPERATING NORMAL AT THIS TIME.  AT APPROXIMATELY 8:32 PM ON SEPTEMBER 26, 2006, #4 COMPRESSOR UNIT SHUTS-DOWN FOR A SECOND TIME DUE TO AN OVER-SPEED CONDITION.  COMPRESSOR OPERATOR PURGES AIR INTAKE AND ATTEMPTS TO RESTART THE COMPRESSOR UNIT WHEN THE EXPLOSION OCCURRED.  EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN DEVICES WERE ACTIVATED AUTOMATICALLY BY STATION FIRE ALARMS AND MANUALLY BY DOMINION EAST OHIO GAS PERSONNEL ON SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 8:48 PM. AN IGNITON LOCK-OUT TIMER HAS BEEN INSTALLED TO PREVENT IGNITION FROM BEING OPERATED PRIOR TO A TEN-SECOND PURGE OF THE AIR INTAKE, THIS IS AN INCREASE FROM A MANUAL 3-5 SECOND COUNT PRIOR TO IGNITION.  AN ADDITIONAL 3 OF 2" PIPE HAS BEEN INSTALLED ON THE VENTS TO PROVIDE ADDITIONAL SAFETY FOR GAS BEING VENTED FROM THE COMPRESSORS. narrative_clean: on september 26, 2006 at approximately 8:42 pm a fire/explosion occured at dominion east ohio's robinson compressor facility located at 5433 west blvd in canton, oh. emergency shutdown devices were activated automatically by station fire alarms and maually by dominion eastohio gas personnel on site at approximately 8:48 pm shutting down all four reciprocating compressors at the facility. a courtesy call was made to the public tilities commission of ohio at 9:30 pm on september 26,2006 until damage assessment could be conducted to determine the origin of the explosion and amount of property damages. preliminary damage assessment indicated damage to the #4 compressor unit air intake, scavenging unitl lower convers on #4 and #5 compressor cylinders and the turbo-charger. all four compressor units remained shut-down for the night until further investigation. an investigation ws conducted by dominion east ohio and the public utilities commission of ohio on september 27, 2006 at approximately 3:00 pm to the national response center and to the public utilities commission of ohio by telephone. nrc #812542 was assighned to this event at that time. further investigation revealed that the #4 compressor unit had shut down on september 26, 2006 at approximately 6:58 pm due to an over-speed condition. the compressor operator attempted to re-start the unit, the unit backfired. the compressor ooperator suspected fuel in the air intake, purged the intake with air and re-started the unit. jackson township fire department responded to an explosion call from a local resident at approximately 7:30 pm. fire department personnel spoke with the compressor operator and determined the resident had heard the back-fire of #4 compressor unit. all four compressors operating normal at this time. at approximately 8:32 pm on september 26, 2006, #4 compressor unit shuts-down for a second time due to an over-speed condition. compressor operator purges air intake and THIS EMPLOYEE IMMEDIATELY RESPONDED TO THE CALL AND ARRIVED AT THE MILL SPRING TAKE-OFF STATION AT 7:00 P.M.  THE PSNC ENERGY TAKE-OFF STATION WAS ON FIRE.    THE FIRE WAS OF A MAGNITUDE AND IN A LOCATION THAT THE PSNC ENERGY STATION VALVES COULD NOT BE REACHED.  PSNC ENERGY ENGINEERING AND OPERATIONS PERSONNEL DEVELOPED A PLAN TO ISOLATE THE TAKE-OFF STATION UTILIZING OTHER REMOTE PIPELINE BLOCK VALVES.  FIRE FIGHTERS USED WATER BLANKETS TO KEEP OTHER EQUIPMENT, SURROUNDING MATERIALS, AND VEGETATION FROM COMBUSTING.    AT 9:55 P.M. THE TAKE-OFF STATION WAS ISOLATED AND THE FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED.    BASED UPON THE LOCAL SEVERE WEATHER CONDITIONS AND FIRST-HAND ACCOUNTS, PSNC ENERGY'S SCADA SYSTEM ALARMS, AND POST-INCIDENT SITE EVALUATIONS, IT IS BELIEVED THAT LIGHTNING CAUSED A TUBING FAILURE WHICH SUBSEQUENTLY RESULTED IN A STATION FIRE.
narrative_clean: psnc energy's mill spring take-off station is located on a site owned and operated by williams-transco in mill spring, north carolina. on april 8, 2010, psnc energy's scada system indicated a low pressure alarm from the mill spring take-off station at 6:42 p.m. followed by a high flow alarm at 6:47 p.m. psnc energy's gas control dispatched company personnel to this site to investigate the alarm notifications. about the same time, residents in the vicinity of the mill spring take-off station reported seeing bright lightning and immediate thunder. simultaneous with the scada alarms, at approximately 6:40 p.m., a local psnc energy employee received calls from the polk county sherriff's department and polk county ems indicating a fire at the mill spring take-off station. this employee immediately responded to the call and arrived at the mill spring take-off station at 7:00 p.m. the psnc energy take-off station was on fire. the fire was of a magnitude and in a location that the psnc energy station valves could not be reached. psnc energy engineering and operations personnel developed a plan to isolate the take-off station utilizing other remote pipeline block valves. fire fighters used water blankets to keep other equipment, surrounding materials, and vegetation from combusting. at 9:55 p.m. the take-off station was isolated and the fire was extinguished. based upon the local severe weather conditions and first-hand accounts, psnc energy's scada system alarms, and post-incident site evaluations, it is believed that lightning caused a tubing failure which subsequently resulted in a station fire.

NARRATIVE: THE 16" STEEL GAS MAIN INCURRED A PARTIAL CIRCUMFERENTIAL BREAK. PRESSURE & MEASUREMENT DEPARTMENT CLOSED ISOLATION VALVES, LOWERED PRESSURES ON THE SYSTEM FROM 222 PSIG TO 35 PSIG. CAUSE OF THE DAMAGE IS UNKNOWN AND STILL UNDER INVESTIGATION.    SUPPLEMENTAL REPORT DATA (4/13/12): MISSOURI PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION FILED A REPORT DEC. 9, 2011 (CASE NO. GS-2011-0248), BASED ON THEIR SAFETY STAFF'S RECOMMENDATIONS. MGE AND MPSC SAFETY STAFF AGREED THAT MGE WILL REPLACE THE ENTIRE LENGTH OF THE MAYFAIR 16 INCH PIPELINE IN TWO PHASES. PHASE 1 WILL REPLACE THE SECTION WHERE THE INCIDENT OCCURRED AND WILL BE COMPLETED BETWEEN JUNE 1, 2012 AND OCTOBER 1, 2012. ONCE THE PIPELINE IS REMOVED FROM SERVICE, MGE WILL REMOVE THE REPAIRED SECTION OF PIPE THAT CAUSED THE ORIGINAL INCIDENT AND PERFORM AN INVESTIGATION OF THE FRACTURE TO DETERMINE THE CAUSE. NO OTHER DATA HAS BEEN DISCOVERED, TO DATE, TO DETERMIN THE CAUSE OF THE FRACTURE.    FINAL REPORT DATA (3/28/2013):  MGE COMPLETED REPLACEMENT OF THIS SECTION OF 16 INCH STEEL MAIN ON 11/06/2012. THE SECTION OF PIPE THAT CAUSED THE ORIGINAL INCIDENT WAS CUT OUT AND REMOVED FROM THE GROUND AND SENT FOR METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS. THE CONCLUSION FROM THE DATA COLLECTED FROM THE SCANNING ELECTRON MICROSCOPE (SEM) AND METALLOGRAPHIC WORK IS THAT THE FAILURE MECHANISM IS STRESS CORROSION CRACKING (SCC) WHICH RESULTED FROM SETTLEMENT OF THE SOIL UNDER THE 16 INCH STEEL GAS MAIN THAT WAS INSTALLED IN 1997, RESULTING IN A SIGNIFICANT TORSIONAL LOAD ON THE PIPE APPROXIMATELY 13 FEET TO THE WEST (POINT OF BREAK).

narrative_clean: the compressor station emergency shutdown (esd) was caused by a control panel lock up. when the station esd occurred, the station discharge valve failed to close. the inactivation of the valve resulted in natural gas to vent from the pipeline until technicians responded and manually closed the station blowdown valve to stop the release of gas. the valve was closed approximately 40 minutes after the esd. troubleshoot components on valve operator. operation was tested numerous times and functioned as designed.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION CORP
NARRATIVE: AT 16:04 ON FRIDAY, MAY 13, 2011, A POSSIBLE FIRE WAS REPORTED BY COLUMBIA'S MONITORING CENTER.  THE EVENT WAS AT THE COMPANY'S STATION CAMP COMPRESSOR STATION, A SMALL UNMANNED STATION IN RURAL CENTRAL KENTUCKY.  THE STATION CONSISTS OF FOUR AJAX 230 HORSEPOWER UNITS.    THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS ON SITE AND HAD CLOSED A ROAD ADJACENT TO THE STATION.  COMPANY EMPLOYEES HAD ARRIVED AT THE SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 16:00 AND CONFIRMED THAT UNIT #3 WAS ON FIRE.  BY 16:35 THE STATION WAS SHUT IN AND THE FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED.    AFTER A THOROUGH EXAMINATION, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT ONLY UNIT #3 HAD BEEN DAMAGED.  IT WAS DECLARED TO BE UNAVAILABLE FOR SERVICE, PENDING FURTHER ASSESSMENT AND REPAIR.  THE OTHER UNITS WERE LATER RETURNED TO SERVICE WITHOUT INCIDENT.    THE UNITS AT THIS STATION ARE OWNED BY EXTERRAN AND LEASED TO COLUMBIA.  A REPRESENTATIVE OF EXTERRAN ARRIVED AT THE SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 18:45 AND PROVIDED AN INITIAL DAMAGE ESTIMATE OF $125,000 TO $250,000.  THIS ESTIMATE WAS RECEIVED AT APPROXIMATELY 19:02.  UPON RECEIPT OF THIS ESTIMATE, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT AN INCIDENT HAD OCCURRED.  THE NRC AND PHMSA SOUTHERN REGION OFFICES WERE NOTIFIED AT 19:44 AND 20:08 RESPECTIVELY.     OVER THE COURSE OF THE NEXT THREE DAYS THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE EVENT WERE ESTABLISHED.  IT WAS DECIDED THAT THE COMPRESSOR CROSSHEAD SLIDE HAD FAILED AND SIEZED ON UNIT #3.  THE RESULTANT HEAT AND DAMAGE IGNITED CRANKCASE OIL VAPORS (VIA THE OIL BREATHER) AND A NEARBY LUBE OIL DAY STORAGE TANK.  THE HEAT FROM THE OIL FIRE HAD, IN TURN, DAMAGED A VALVE IN THE STARTING GAS SYSTEM, CAUSING GAS LEAKAGE AND A SUBSEQUENT SMALL SECONDARY FIRE.  THIS SECONDARY FIRE CAUSED NO APPARENT ADDITIONAL DAMAGE.    REPAIRS WERE MADE TO THE UNIT AND IT WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON MAY 27.  FINAL REPAIR COSTS TOTALLED APPROXIMATELY $120,000.
narrative_clean: at 16:04 on friday, may 13, 2011, a possible fire was reported by columbia's monitoring center. the event was at the company's station camp compressor station, a small unmanned station in rural central kentucky. the station consists of four ajax 230 horsepower units. the local fire department was on site and had closed a road adjacent to the station. company employees had arrived at the site at approximately 16:00 and confirmed that unit #3 was on fire. by 16:35 the station was shut in and the fire was extinguished. after a thorough examination, it was determined that only unit #3 had been damaged. it was declared to be unavailable for service, pending further assessment and repair. the other units were later returned to service without incident. the units at this station are owned by exterran and leased to columbia. a representative of exterran arrived at the site at approximately 18:45 and provided an initial damage estimate of $125,000 to $250,000. this estimate was received at approximately 19:02. upon receipt of this estimate, it was determined that an incident had occurred. the nrc and phmsa southern region offices were notified at 19:44 and 20:08 respectively. over the course of the next three days the circumstances of the event were established. it was decided that the compressor crosshead slide had failed and siezed on unit #3. the resultant heat and damage ignited crankcase oil vapors (via the oil breather) and a nearby lube oil day storage tank. the heat from the oil fire had, in turn, damaged a valve in the starting gas system, causing gas leakage and a subsequent small secondary fire. this secondary fire caused no apparent additional damage. repairs were made to the unit and it was returned to service on may 27. final repair costs totalled approximately $120,000.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE CO (EL PASO)
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE (TGP) WAS NOTIFIED ON JUNE 14, 2011, BY BOEMRE AND BY A PRODUCER, STONE ENERGY, OF BUBBLES ON THE OCS IN BAY MAR BLOCK 5, THE COORDINATES OF WHICH INDICATED THEY WERE COMING FROM TGP'S PIPELINE FACILITY.  UPON INVESTIGATION, DIVERS REMOVED PROTECTIVE MATS FROM A SUBSEA TIE-IN ASSEMBLY ON TGP'S 524C-400 PIPELINE AND FOUND A CRACK IN THE NECK OF A 2" FLANGE THAT WAS PART OF THE TIE-IN OF AN INTERSECTING PIPELINE.  REPAIRS WERE MADE AND THE PIPELINE FACILITY WAS PLACED BACK INTO SERVICE.  METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS CONCLUDED THAT THE CRACK IN THE WELD OF THE 2" FLANGE WAS LIKELY DUE TO OVERLOAD FRACTURE DUE TO EXTERNAL BENDING AND/OR TENSILE FORCES.  SUCH FORCES WERE POSSIBLY CAUSED BY INSTABILITY OF THE SUBSEA FLOOR AND CONCRETE MATS PLACED OVER ASSEMBLY AT TIME OF CONSTRUCTION.  YEAR OF PIPE MANUFACTURE IS ASSUMED TO BE COMMENSURATE WITH YEAR OF INSTALLATION.
narrative_clean: tennessee gas pipeline (tgp) was notified on june 14, 2011, by boemre and by a producer, stone energy, of bubbles on the ocs in bay mar block 5, the coordinates of which indicated they were coming from tgp's pipeline facility. upon investigation, divers removed protective mats from a subsea tie-in assembly on tgp's 524c-400 pipeline and found a crack in the neck of a 2" flange that was part of the tie-in of an intersecting pipeline. repairs were made and the pipeline facility was placed back into service. metallurgical analysis concluded that the crack in the weld of the 2" flange was likely due to overload fracture due to external bending and/or tensile forces. such forces were possibly caused by instability of the subsea floor and concrete mats placed over assembly at time of construction. year of pipe manufacture is assumed to be commensurate with year of installation.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION CORP
NARRATIVE: A 4-IN RELIEF VALVE (RV) HAD FAILED WHERE IT RELIEVED NATURAL GAS INTO ATMOSPHERE BEFORE REACHING ITS SET POINT AT PAVONIA COMPRESSOR STATION, OH.  TOTAL AMOUNT OF NATURAL GAS RELEASED INTO ATMOSPHERE WAS CALCULATED TO BE 9,303 MCF. A QUALITY INVESTIGATION CONSULTANT CONDUCTED A FULL ANALYSIS TO THE FAILED RV AND PROVIDED A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS DETAILING THE FOLLOWING:    A DESTRUCTIVE/NON-DESTRUCTIVE TEST WAS PERFORMED TO THE REMOVED SOFT GOODS FROM THE FAILED RV AT A CERTIFIED RUBBER LABORATORY FACILITY WHERE IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT THE USED SOFT GOODS WERE PER THE MANUFACTURER'S RECOMMENDED MATERIAL LIST.  A NEWLY PUBLISHED MAINTENANCE MANUAL OF THE FAILED RV PROVIDED ONLINE BY THE MANUFACTURER INDICATED THAT THE PRESSURE RATINGS FOR THE INSTALLED PILOT VALVE WERE REDUCED TO A LOWER LEVEL FOR ALL DIAPHRAGM-TYPE INSTALLATIONS.  ALL HIGHER PRESSURE VALUES ABOVE THE ASSIGNED THRESHOLD MUST GO TO A PISTON-TYPE PILOT INSTALLATION.  THIS INFORMATION THAT WAS RELEVANT TO THE PILOT VALVE WAS NOT PROVIDED TO THE MAINTENANCE FACILITY HENCE IT WAS NOT IMPLEMENTED ONTO THE FAILED RV.      AN IN-HOUSE MEMORANDUM WAS ISSUED TO SEARCH FOR ALL SIMILAR INSTALLATIONS TO THE FAILED RV. A SIMILAR INSTALLATION WAS IDENTIFIED AT THE SAME FACILITY AND WAS REMOVED.  A DIFFERENT TYPE OF RVS WAS INSTALLED AND NEW CAPACITY CALCULATIONS AND VERIFICATIONS WERE COMPLETED AND THE FACILITY WAS RETURNED BACK TO SERVICE.
narrative_clean: a 4-in relief valve (rv) had failed where it relieved natural gas into atmosphere before reaching its set point at pavonia compressor station, oh. total amount of natural gas released into atmosphere was calculated to be 9,303 mcf. a quality investigation consultant conducted a full analysis to the failed rv and provided a root cause analysis detailing the following: a destructive/non-destructive test was performed to the removed soft goods from the failed rv at a certified rubber laboratory facility where it was confirmed that the used soft goods were per the manufacturer's recommended material list. a newly published maintenance manual of the failed rv provided online by the manufacturer indicated that the pressure ratings for the installed pilot valve were reduced to a lower level for all diaphragm-type installations. all higher pressure values above the assigned threshold must go to a piston-type pilot installation. this information that was relevant to the pilot valve was not provided to the maintenance facility hence it was not implemented onto the failed rv. an in-house memorandum was issued to search for all similar installations to the failed rv. a similar installation was identified at the same facility and was removed. a different type of rvs was installed and new capacity calculations and verifications were completed and the facility was returned back to service.

NAME: WILLISTON BASIN INTERSTATE PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: A DOWNSTREAM STATION REGULATOR #6 (R6) WENT CLOSED DUE TO THE WARM NIGHT TEMPERATURES WHICH REQUIRED A MINIMAL AMOUNT OF GAS TO HOLD THE BILLINGS LINE.  THE UPSTREAM REGULATOR #5 (R5)WAS LEAKING ENOUGH GAS TO CREATE AN EXCESS PRESSURE BUILD UP ON THE "SHUT-IN" DRY BED DEHY INLET PIPING.  RELIEF VALVE #12 (RV12) OPENED AS DESIGNED AT A SCADA REPORTED PRESSURE OF 719 PSIG TO PROTECT THE MAOP (720 PSIG) OF THE DRY BED DEHY PIPING.  AFTER THE RELIEF VALVE OPENED RELEASING GAS, A 1/4 INCH PIPE NIPPLE BROKE OFF ON THE RELIEF VALVE PIPING SUPPLYING PILOT GAS TO THE RELIEF VALVE.  THE PIPE NIPPLE THAT FAILED SUPPLIED PILOT GAS TO THE RELIEF VALVE WHICH RESULTED IN LOST PILOT PRESSURE AND PREVENTED THE RELIEF VALVE FROM RESEATING.  ONCE THE OPERATOR REACHED THE STATION, THE DEHY PRESSURE WAS VERIFIED AND THE VALVE SUPPLYING GAS TO THE RELIEF VALVE AND PILOT VALVE WAS CLOSED.  THE DEHY WAS THEN SHUT IN.  ACCORDING TO SCADA TRENDING, GAS VENTED FOR 1 HR AND 15 MINUTES.  THE ESTIMATED VOLUME RELEASED WAS CALCULATED TO BE APPROXIMATELY 3,800 MCF WHICH EXCEEDS THE REPORTABLE INCIDENT THRESHOLD OF 3,000 MCF.  THE OVERPRESSURE CONDITION RESULTED FROM A LEAKING REGULATOR, NOT BY ACTIONS OF THE GAS CONTROLLER OR STATION PERSONNEL.  GAS CONTROL DOES NOT HAVE SUPERVISORY CONTROL OF ANY STATION REGULATORS AND THE STATION WAS UNATTENDED AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT.  THE PIR CALCULATED IN THIS REPORT WAS BASED ON A 3" BLOW DOWN STACK AND 720 PSIG MAOP.    APPENDED PART E5F TO TRANSMISSION SYSTEM PER DOT EMAIL REQUEST FROM BLAINE KEENER ON 3/4/13.
narrative_clean: a downstream station regulator #6 (r6) went closed due to the warm night temperatures which required a minimal amount of gas to hold the billings line. the upstream regulator #5 (r5)was leaking enough gas to create an excess pressure build up on the "shut-in" dry bed dehy inlet piping. relief valve #12 (rv12) opened as designed at a scada reported pressure of 719 psig to protect the maop (720 psig) of the dry bed dehy piping. after the relief valve opened releasing gas, a 1/4 inch pipe nipple broke off on the relief valve piping supplying pilot gas to the relief valve. the pipe nipple that failed supplied pilot gas to the relief valve which resulted in lost pilot pressure and prevented the relief valve from reseating. once the operator reached the station, the dehy pressure was verified and the valve supplying gas to the relief valve and pilot valve was closed. the dehy was then shut in. according to scada trending, gas vented for 1 hr and 15 minutes. the estimated volume released was calculated to be approximately 3,800 mcf which exceeds the reportable incident threshold of 3,000 mcf. the overpressure condition resulted from a leaking regulator, not by actions of the gas controller or station personnel. gas control does not have supervisory control of any station regulators and the station was unattended at the time of the incident. the pir calculated in this report was based on a 3" blow down stack and 720 psig maop. appended part e5f to transmission system per dot email request from blaine keener on 3/4/13.

NAME: ENOGEX LLC
NARRATIVE: PRIOR TO THE INCIDENT ON 11/19/2011 A SEGMENT OF L-4 BETWEEN N/E/ TAP AND KEETONVILLE YARD HAD BEEN REMOVED FROM SERVICE FOR ILI REMEDIATION AND REPAIRS.  THIS OUTAGE REQUIRED GAS TO BE RE-ROUTED FROM NEPS AT OOLAHGA, OK DOWN L-4 TO THE L-4 TO L-4A JUNCTION AT KEETONVILLE, OK TO CONTINUE THE SUPPLY OF GAS THROUGH L-4A & L-4B TO CUSTOMERS CONNECTED TO L-4C INSIDE THE PRYOR INDUSTRIAL PARK.  ON 11/18/2011, THE CLAREMORE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS REMOVED FROM SERVICE FOR MAINTENANCE OF MEASUREMENT EQUIPMENT.  THIS OUTAGE ELIMINATED THE USE OF L-4A AND L-4B TO SUPPLY GAS TO L-4C; THEREBY REQUIRING THE USE OF AN ALTERNATE VALVE INSIDE THE AECI GAS YARD AT CHOTEAU, OK TO ROUTE GAS FROM L-281 INTO L-4E TO SUPPLY GAS TO CUSTOMERS CONNECTED TO L-4C INSIDE THE PRYOR INDUSTRIAL PARK.  THE FLOW OF GAS FROM L-281 INTO L-4E TO SUPPLY GAS TO L-4C HAD NOT BEEN ATTEMPTED PRIOR TO THIS DATE.  DUE TO THE GAS LOAD AT THE TWO POWER PLANTS AT AECI AND THE DEMAND REQUIRED BY CUSTOMERS IN THE PRYOR INDUSTRIAL PARK, IT WAS DETERMINED THAT PCV-281 IN THE AECI GAS YARD COULD NOT SUPPLY THE AMOUNT OF GAS NECESSARY.  XV-102, A 16' VALVE WAS OPENED BY GAS CONTROL TO BYPASS GAS FLOW AROUND PCV-281 AND SUPPLEMENT THE FLOW THROUGH PCV-281.  AT AN UNKNOWN TIME ON THE EVENING OF 11/18/2011, THE AECI POWER PLANT REDUCED THE DEMAND LOAD INTO THE POWER PLANTS.  GAS FLOW THEN TOOK THE PATH OF LEAST RESISTANCE, WHICH WAS INTO L-4E AND L-4C.  GAS FLOW CONTINUED TO FLOW BACKWARD INTO L-4B TOWARD THE CLAREMORE COMPRESSOR STATION.  PC-6, A RECYCLE/SURGE CONTROL VALVE INSIDE THE CLAREMORE STATION, DETECTED THE INCREASING PRESSURE IN L-4B AND OPENED AT A SETPOINT OF 750 PSIG, THEREBY ROUTING GAS AROUND THE CLAREMORE STATION INTO L-4A.  THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS NOT NEEDED AND THEREFORE NOT OPERATING AT THIS TIME.  THIS GAS FLOW CONTINUED TO FLOW INTO L-4, THUS STEADILY INCREASING THE PRESSURE IN L-4 UNTIL THE SETPOINT ON AVAILABLE OVERPRESSURE WAS SATISFIED AND THE PSV AT THE NEPS GAS YARD ACTIVATED.  THE NEPS CONTROL ROOM OPERATOR INITIALLY NOTIFIED AN ONG REPRESENTATIVE TO RESPOND TO GAS VENTING IN THE GAS YARD.  UPON ARRIVAL, THE ONG INDICATED TO THE NEPS CONTROL ROOM THAT THE GAS RELEASE WAS FROM A ENOGEX PSV.  THE NEPS CONTROL ROOM OPERATOR THEN IMMEDIATELY NOTIFIED ENOGEX GAS CONTROL AT 1:40 AM.  THE ENOGEX ON-CALL PERSONNEL ARRIVED AT NEPS AT 3:00 AM AND IMMEDIATELY CONFIRMED WITH GAS CONTROL THAT THE L-4 OPERATING PRESSURE WAS 369 PSIG OR 236 PSIG BELOW THE MAOP OF 605.  THE PSV WAS THEN ISOLATED TO END THE RELEASE OF GAS AND GAS CONTROL WAS INSTRUCTED TO CLOSE XV-102 IN THE AECI GAS YARD AT CHOTEAU.  THE ENOGEX ON-CALL PERSONNEL THEN DROVE TO THE CLAREMORE COMPRESSOR STATION TO ISOLATE PV-6 TO STOP THE FLOW OF GAS INTO L-4A.  THE ENOGEX ON-CALL PERSONNEL THEN RETURNED TO NEPS TO PLACE THE PSV BACK INTO SERVICE.  AN INSPECTION OF THE PSV AT NEPS GAS YARD REVEALED MINOR SCARRING OF THE SEAT MATERIAL THAT PREVENTED THE PSV FROM AUTOMATICALLY RESEATING ONCE THE L-4 PRESSURE FELL BELOW THE PSV SETPOINT OF 605.  AN INVESTIGATION OF THIS INCIDENT REVEALED THAT PV-6 LOCATED IN THE CLAREMORE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS PROGRAMMED TO OPEN WHEN THE COMPRESSOR DISCHARGE PRESSURE IS EQUAL TO OR GREATER THAN 750 PSIG.  IT WAS ALSO DETERMINED THAT THE PV-6 SURGE VALVE IS NOT NEEDED WHEN THE COMPRESSORS ARE NOT RUNNING.  A CHANGE IN THE CONTROL LOGIC PROGRAM AT THE CLAREMORE COMPRESSOR STATION IS SCHEDULED FOR DECEMBER 22, 2011 TO INTERLOCK THE OPERATION OF PV-6 WHEN THE COMPRESSORS ARE NOT RUNNING OR DURING AN ESD CONDITION.  THIS WILL PREVENT PV-6 FROM ROUTING GAS FROM L-4B INTO L-4A AND INTO L-4.  UPDATE MARCH 5, 2013: COMPLETED SECTION E.5.F.
narrative_clean: prior to the incident on 11/19/2011 a segment of l-4 between n/e/ tap and keetonville yard had been removed from service for ili remediation and repairs. this outage required gas to be re-routed from neps at oolahga, ok down l-4 to the l-4 to l-4a junction at keetonville, ok to continue the supply of gas through l-4a & l-4b to customers connected to l-4c inside the pryor industrial park. on 11/18/2011, the claremore compressor station was removed from service for maintenance of measurement equipment. this outage eliminated the use of l-4a and l-4b to supply gas to l-4c; thereby requiring the use of an alternate valve inside the aeci gas yard at choteau, ok to route gas from l-281 into l-4e to supply gas to customers connected to l-4c inside the pryor industrial park. the flow of gas from l-281 into l-4e to supply gas to l-4c had not been attempted prior to this date. due to the gas load at the two power plants at aeci and the demand required by customers in the pryor industrial park, it was determined that pcv-281 in the aeci gas yard could not supply the amount of gas necessary. xv-102, a 16' valve was opened by gas control to bypass gas flow around pcv-281 and supplement the flow through pcv-281. at an unknown time on the evening of 11/18/2011, the aeci power plant reduced the demand load into the power plants. gas flow then took the path of least resistance, which was into l-4e and l-4c. gas flow continued to flow backward into l-4b toward the claremore compressor station. pc-6, a recycle/surge control valve inside the claremore station, detected the increasing pressure in l-4b and opened at a setpoint of 750 psig, thereby routing gas around the claremore station into l-4a. the compressor station was not needed and therefore not operating at this time. this gas flow continued to flow into l-4, thus steadily increasing the pressure in l-4 until the setpoint on available overpressure was satisfied and the psv at the neps gas yard activated. the neps control room operator initially notified an ong representative to respond to gas venting in the gas yard. upon arrival, the ong indicated to the neps control room that the gas release was from a enogex psv. the neps control room operator then immediately notified enogex gas control at 1:40 am. the enogex on-call personnel arrived at neps at 3:00 am and immediately confirmed with gas control that the l-4 operating pressure was 369 psig or 236 psig below the maop of 605. the psv was then isolated to end the release of gas and gas control was instructed to close xv-102 in the aeci gas yard at choteau. the enogex on-call personnel then drove to the claremore compressor station to isolate pv-6 to stop the flow of gas into l-4a. the enogex on-call personnel then returned to neps to place the psv back into service. an inspection of the psv at neps gas yard revealed minor scarring of the seat material that prevented the psv from automatically reseating once the l-4 pressure fell below the psv setpoint of 605. an investigation of this incident revealed that pv-6 located in the claremore compressor station was programmed to open when the compressor discharge pressure is equal to or greater than 750 psig. it was also determined that the pv-6 surge valve is not needed when the compressors are not running. a change in the control logic program at the claremore compressor station is scheduled for december 22, 2011 to interlock the operation of pv-6 when the compressors are not running or during an esd condition. this will prevent pv-6 from routing gas from l-4b into l-4a and into l-4. update march 5, 2013: completed section e.5.f.

NAME: VIRGINIA NATURAL GAS
CAUSE_DETAILS: EARTH MOVEMENT, NOT DUE TO HEAVY RAINS/FLOODS
NARRATIVE: VIRGINIA NATURAL GAS EMPLOYEES SMELLED GAS WHILE PERFORMING ROUTINE MAINTENANCE AT THE LADYSMITH M&R STATION (M&R-143) ON 01/18/12.  ALL ABOVE GROUND PIPING AND EQUIPMENT WAS IMMEDIATELY INVESTIGATED AT THE SITE AND NO LEAKS WERE FOUND.  VNG CALLED IN A MISS UTILITY LOCATE TICKET TO EXCAVATE IN THE AREA TO SEARCH FOR THE POTENTIAL LEAK.  THE TICKET WAS CLEARED AND EXCAVATION BEGAN ON 01/23/12.  A SMALL LEAK WAS FOUND AT THE 24 INCH WELD-END INSULATOR THAT WAS NEAR THE LADYSMITH M&R STATION.  VNG NOTIFIED THE VIRGINIA STATE CORPORATION COMMISSION OF THE FOUND LEAK AND BEGAN STAGING EQUIPMENT, MATERIAL AND LABOR TO MAKE THE REPAIR.  THE AFFECTED SECTION OF PIPELINE WAS ISOLATED BY CLOSING MLV-140 AND MLV-145, AND THE 2-MILE SECTION OF 24 INCH PIPELINE WAS PURGED OF GAS.  AFTER THE SECTION OF PIPELINE WAS FREE OF GAS, THE FAILED INSULATOR WAS REMOVED AND A LENGTH OF PRE-TESTED PIPE WAS INSTALLED.  THE PIPELINE WAS RE-ACTIVATED ON 01/25/12.  IT IS NOTED THAT THE WEATHER WAS MILD AND DOWNSTREAM CUSTOMERS HAD ALTERNATE SOURCES OF FUEL TO OPERATE AND/OR DID NOT NEED TO OPERATE.  THE FAILED 24 INCH WELD-END INSULATOR WAS SHIPPED TO AN INDEPENDENT, THIRD-PARTY LABORATORY FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATION.      THE INDEPENDENT LABORATORY CONCLUDED THAT THE INSULATOR SUFFERED EITHER A SINGLE, SEVERE BENDING MOMENT OR SEVERAL, SUCCESSIVE, LESS CATASTROPHIC BENDING MOMENTS THAT CAUSED THE INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR EPOXY TO CRACK AND OPEN A PATH AT THE CENTER GASKET FOR MATERIAL TO ESCAPE.  THE ONLY KNOWN PHYSICAL OR ENVIRONMENTAL FACTOR THAT COULD HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO THE FAILURE OF THE FITTING IS THE EARTHQUAKE THAT OCCURRED IN VIRGINIA ON AUGUST 23, 2011.
narrative_clean: virginia natural gas employees smelled gas while performing routine maintenance at the ladysmith m&r station (m&r-143) on 01/18/12. all above ground piping and equipment was immediately investigated at the site and no leaks were found. vng called in a miss utility locate ticket to excavate in the area to search for the potential leak. the ticket was cleared and excavation began on 01/23/12. a small leak was found at the 24 inch weld-end insulator that was near the ladysmith m&r station. vng notified the virginia state corporation commission of the found leak and began staging equipment, material and labor to make the repair. the affected section of pipeline was isolated by closing mlv-140 and mlv-145, and the 2-mile section of 24 inch pipeline was purged of gas. after the section of pipeline was free of gas, the failed insulator was removed and a length of pre-tested pipe was installed. the pipeline was re-activated on 01/25/12. it is noted that the weather was mild and downstream customers had alternate sources of fuel to operate and/or did not need to operate. the failed 24 inch weld-end insulator was shipped to an independent, third-party laboratory for further investigation. the independent laboratory concluded that the insulator suffered either a single, severe bending moment or several, successive, less catastrophic bending moments that caused the interior and exterior epoxy to crack and open a path at the center gasket for material to escape. the only known physical or environmental factor that could have contributed to the failure of the fitting is the earthquake that occurred in virginia on august 23, 2011.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE CO (EL PASO)
NARRATIVE: NATURAL GAS WAS RELEASED AT TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE (TGP) COMPANY'S COMPRESSOR STATION 249 FROM UNIT 1A WHEN A COMPRESSOR ROD FAILED IN ITS THREADS. A ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS DETERMINED THAT THE FAILURE WAS LIKELY DUE TO A COMBINATION OF FACTORS, INCLUDING HIGH CYCLE LOW NOMINAL STRESS AXIAL FATIGUE, INSUFFICIENT TIGHTENING DURING THE LATEST MAINTENANCE ACTIVITY, AND THE PRESENCE OF LOWER STRENGTH MATERIAL NOT MEETING THE CHEMISTRY AND MECHANICAL PROPERTY REQUIREMENTS OF THE SPECIFICATION FOR NEW REPLACEMENT COMPRESSOR RODS.
narrative_clean: natural gas was released at tennessee gas pipeline (tgp) company's compressor station 249 from unit 1a when a compressor rod failed in its threads. the station's esd system activated and evacuated the station of natural gas. the unit has been repaired and is back in service. a root cause analysis determined that the failure was likely due to a combination of factors, including high cycle low nominal stress axial fatigue, insufficient tightening during the latest maintenance activity, and the presence of lower strength material not meeting the chemistry and mechanical property requirements of the specification for new replacement compressor rods.

NAME: EQT MIDSTREAM
NARRATIVE: AT APPROXIMATELY 1:12 AM APRIL 7, 2012 GAS CONTROL RECEIVED AN ALARM FOR COPLEY COMPRESSOR STATION (544 COPLEY ROAD, WESTON, WV 26452-7174) UNIT #5 COMPRESSOR SHUT DOWN.  GAS CONTROL IMMEDIATELY CONTACTED THE ON-CALL EQT COMPRESSOR TECHNICIAN WHO REPORTED TO THE SITE.  THE COPLEY STATION ESD TRIPPED AT APPROXIMATELY 1:48 AM WHILE THE COMPRESSOR TECHNICIAN WAS EN ROUTE.  THE COMPRESSOR TECHNICIAN ARRIVED AT THE SITE AT APPROXIMATELY 2:03 AM AND DETERMINED ALL ESD VALVES DID NOT CLOSE AND GAS WAS VENTING TO THE ATMOSPHERE.  THE COMPRESSOR TECHNICIAN PROCEEDED TO SHUT OFF ONE BLOCK VALVE THAT WAS 100% OPEN AND TWO BLOCK VALVES THAT WERE 20% OPEN.  THE VALVES WERE CLOSED AND GAS SHUT OFF AT APPROXIMATELY 2:08 AM. THERE WAS NOT ENOUGH SUPPLY AIR IN THE SYSTEM TO FULLY SHUT THREE OF THE ESD VALVES.  DESIGN ENGINEERING CALCULATED THE GAS LOSS TO BE 11.2 MMCF WHICH REQUIRED AN INCIDENT REPORT FILING.
narrative_clean: at approximately 1:12 am april 7, 2012 gas control received an alarm for copley compressor station (544 copley road, weston, wv 26452-7174) unit #5 compressor shut down. gas control immediately contacted the on-call eqt compressor technician who reported to the site. the copley station esd tripped at approximately 1:48 am while the compressor technician was en route. the compressor technician arrived at the site at approximately 2:03 am and determined all esd valves did not close and gas was venting to the atmosphere. the compressor technician proceeded to shut off one block valve that was 100% open and two block valves that were 20% open. the valves were closed and gas shut off at approximately 2:08 am. eqt facilities engineering investigated and determined two of three air compressors that hold the copley air system pressure up had shut down on high temperature. the third air compressor could not hold the system up and when the air pressure declined below 100 psig the system went into esd. there was not enough supply air in the system to fully shut three of the esd valves. design engineering calculated the gas loss to be 11.2 mmcf which required an incident report filing.

NAME: ENOGEX LLC
NARRATIVE: ON THE MORNING OF APRIL 3, 2012 A DISRUPTION OF PURCHASED POWER SERVING THE PERRY COMPRESSOR STATION AUTOMATICALLY ACTIVATED THE COMPRESSOR STATION EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD) SYSTEM, WHICH IS DESIGNED IN ACCORDANCE WITH 49 CFR PART 192.167.  THE ESD SYSTEM IS DESIGNED TO ISOLATE THE COMPRESSOR STATION FORM THE INCOMING AND OUTGOING PIPELINES AND VENT ALL GAS INSIDE THE STATION TO A SAFE LOCATION.  THE STATION INLET ESD VALVE FAILED TO CLOSE DUE TO A BLOCKAGE IN THE ESD VALVE ACTUATOR EXHAUST TUBING.  THE BLOCKAGE, WHICH WAS IDENTIFIED AS POLLEN DEPOSITED BY INSECTS INSIDE THE TUBING, PREVENTED THE OPERATING PRESSURE INSIDE THE SPRING OPERATED VALVE ACTUATOR FROM VENTING TO ATMOSPHERE, THUS PREVENTING THE VALVE FROM OPERATING PROPERLY.  THE ESD SYSTEM VENT VALVES DID OPERATE PROPERLY, THEREBY VENTING 3,368 MCF OF NATURAL GAS TO THE ATMOSPHERE UNINTENTIONALLY.  GAS CONTROL DISPATCHED COMPANY PERSONNEL TO THE COMRPESSOR STATION.  THE COMPRESSOR STATION WAS ISOLATED FORM THE PIPELINE VIA A MANUAL ISOLATION VALVE.  THE NATURAL GAS REMAINING INSIDE THE STATION ESD VENT PIPING WAS THEN QUICKLY VENTED TO THE ATMOSPHERE.  THE BLOCKAGE WAS REMOVED FROM THE ACTUATOR EXHAUST PORT TUBING AND THE STATION INLET ESD VALVE WAS RETURNED TO NORMAL OPERATION.  THERE WAS NO DAMAGE TO THE ACTUATOR OR ESD VALVE.  UPDATE MARCH 5, 2013: COMPLETED SECTION E.5.F.
narrative_clean: on the morning of april 3, 2012 a disruption of purchased power serving the perry compressor station automatically activated the compressor station emergency shutdown (esd) system, which is designed in accordance with 49 cfr part 192.167. the esd system is designed to isolate the compressor station form the incoming and outgoing pipelines and vent all gas inside the station to a safe location. the station inlet esd valve failed to close due to a blockage in the esd valve actuator exhaust tubing. the blockage, which was identified as pollen deposited by insects inside the tubing, prevented the operating pressure inside the spring operated valve actuator from venting to atmosphere, thus preventing the valve from operating properly. the esd system vent valves did operate properly, thereby venting 3,368 mcf of natural gas to the atmosphere unintentionally. gas control dispatched company personnel to the comrpessor station. the compressor station was isolated form the pipeline via a manual isolation valve. the natural gas remaining inside the station esd vent piping was then quickly vented to the atmosphere. the blockage was removed from the actuator exhaust port tubing and the station inlet esd valve was returned to normal operation. there was no damage to the actuator or esd valve. update march 5, 2013: completed section e.5.f.
