TECHNICIANS IMMEDIATELY BACKED AWAY FROM THE LOCATION. TECHNICIANS WENT TO BOTH THE UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM VALVE LOCATIONS TO BEGIN ISOLATING THE PIPELINE.     OPERATIONS TECHNICIANS NOTIFIED THE OPS MANAGER AT 15:45, WHO THEN NOTIFIED THE OPS DIRECTOR OF THE SITUATION. A CONFERENCE CALL WAS CONDUCTED (BEGINNING AT 16:00) TO DEVELOP A PLAN TO ISOLATE AND REMEDIATE THE SECTION OF PIPE WITH THE LEAK.     THE NRC (#1367017) WAS NOTIFIED AT 16:21 ON 5/11/2023.  A 48HR NRC NOTIFICATION WAS PLACED AT 12:48 ON 5/14/2023.  A FINAL NRC NOTIFICATION WAS PLACED AT 11:29 ON 5/15/2023; THIS UPDATE WAS TO CLARIFY THAT THE PIPELINE INVOLVED IN THIS LEAK INCIDENT WAS A TRANSMISSION PIPELINE.    A PLAN WAS PUT IN PLACE TO LOWER PRESSURE FROM 728PSIG (THE PRESSURE AT TIME OF DISCOVERY) TO 200PSIG, IN AN EFFORT TO KEEP ANY POTENTIAL FLAME BURNING UNTIL THE EXACT LOCATION OF THE LEAK COULD BE DETERMINED. OPS TECHNICIANS BEGAN BLOWING DOWN THE PIPELINE AT 17:34 AND GOT THE LINE PRESSURE DOWN TO 600PSIG BY 18:11 WHILE CONTRACTORS MOBILIZED TO THE SITE. CONTRACTORS UTILIZED A TRACKHOE WITH AN EXTENDED BOOM TO PULL ROCKS AWAY FROM THE LEAK LOCATION...AS ROCKS WERE PULLED AWAY, THE FLAME/FIRE WAS VISIBLE; AS CONTRACTORS WERE WORKING THE PIPELINE WAS BROUGHT DOWN TO 200PSIG. THE FIRE WAS EXTINGUISHED JUST BEFORE 24:00 ON 5/11/2023. AIR MOVERS WERE THEN UTILIZED TO COMPLETE THE BLOW DOWN.    THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS IDENTIFIED AS EXTERNAL CORROSION (PITTING) AND THE FIRE/FLAME WAS LIKELY IGNITED BY A LIGHTNING STRIKE ON 5/11/2023. A 41' SEGMENT OF PIPE WAS SPOOLED IN TO REMEDIATE THE LEAK LOCATION. THE PIPELINE WAS BROUGHT BACK IN TO SERVICE ON 5/15/2023 AT 16:30.    NO BUILDINGS INTENDED FOR HUMAN OCCUPANCY WERE WITHIN 220 YARDS OF THE SEGMENT AND NO DOMESTIC CUSTOMERS WERE IMPACTED BY THE OUTAGE.
narrative_clean: a possible leak/fire was discovered on 5/11/2023 at 14:03 by operations technicians conducting annual line patrols on line o-470. technicians were changing out sign markers in the o-470 row when they felt heat coming from underneath the rocks that covered pipeline in the row. technicians immediately backed away from the location. technicians went to both the upstream and downstream valve locations to begin isolating the pipeline. operations technicians notified the ops manager at 15:45, who then notified the ops director of the situation. a conference call was conducted (beginning at 16:00) to develop a plan to isolate and remediate the section of pipe with the leak. the nrc (#1367017) was notified at 16:21 on 5/11/2023. a 48hr nrc notification was placed at 12:48 on 5/14/2023. a final nrc notification was placed at 11:29 on 5/15/2023; this update was to clarify that the pipeline involved in this leak incident was a transmission pipeline. a plan was put in place to lower pressure from 728psig (the pressure at time of discovery) to 200psig, in an effort to keep any potential flame burning until the exact location of the leak could be determined. ops technicians began blowing down the pipeline at 17:34 and got the line pressure down to 600psig by 18:11 while contractors mobilized to the site. contractors utilized a trackhoe with an extended boom to pull rocks away from the leak location...as rocks were pulled away, the flame/fire was visible; as contractors were working the pipeline was brought down to 200psig. the fire was extinguished just before 24:00 on 5/11/2023. air movers were then utilized to complete the blow down. the cause of the leak was identified as external corrosion (pitting) and the fire/flame was likely ignited by a lightning strike on 5/11/2023. a 41' segment of pipe was spooled in to remediate the leak location. the pipeline was brought back in to service on 5/15/2023 at 16:30. no buildings intended for human occupancy were within 220 yards of the segment and no domestic customers were impacted by the outage.

CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: AT APPROXIMATELY 8:41 A.M. EASTERN DAYLIGHT TIME ON JULY 25, 2023, CGT'S LINE VB RUPTURED (THE INCIDENT). THE INCIDENT OCCURRED NEAR INTERSTATE HIGHWAY 81 (I-81) IN STRASBURG, VA, AND THE RESULTING FIRE OF THE RELEASED GAS CAUSED I-81 TO CLOSE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS FOR ABOUT TWO HOURS. THE INCIDENT RESULTED IN THE EJECTION OF SEVERAL PIECES OF 26-INCH PIPE, WHICH LANDED ON THE PIPELINE RIGHT-OF-WAY. THERE WERE NO REPORTED INJURIES, FATALITIES, OR EVACUATIONS.    THE LINE VB FAILURE WAS CAUSED BY STRESS CORROSION CRACKING (SCC) DETERMINED BY METALLURGICAL TESTING COMPLETED BY AN INDEPENDENT TESTING FACILITY. THE ROOT CAUSE FAILURE ANALYSIS (RCFA) CONCLUDED THE CAUSE OF THE RUPTURE WAS DUE TO NEAR-NEUTRAL PH (NNPH) SCC BECAUSE OF THE LOCAL CONDITIONS SUPPORTED THE INITIATION AND GROWTH. CONDITIONS INCLUDE THE OPERATING STRESS, SUSCEPTIBLE MATERIAL TYPICAL FOR THE PIPE VINTAGE, THE AREA OF COATING DISBONDMENT AND/OR ROCKY OUTCROP SHIELDING THE PIPE FROM CORROSION PROTECTION, EXTERNAL CORROSION SERVING AS A CRACK RAISER AND THE ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS AT THE PIPE SURFACE PROMOTING THE DEVELOPMENT AND GROWTH PF THE NNPH SCC (E.G. WET-DRY CONDITIONS, NEUTRAL PH, BICARBONATE IONS).
narrative_clean: at approximately 8:41 a.m. eastern daylight time on july 25, 2023, cgt's line vb ruptured (the incident). the incident occurred near interstate highway 81 (i-81) in strasburg, va, and the resulting fire of the released gas caused i-81 to close in both directions for about two hours. the incident resulted in the ejection of several pieces of 26-inch pipe, which landed on the pipeline right-of-way. there were no reported injuries, fatalities, or evacuations. the line vb failure was caused by stress corrosion cracking (scc) determined by metallurgical testing completed by an independent testing facility. the root cause failure analysis (rcfa) concluded the cause of the rupture was due to near-neutral ph (nnph) scc because of the local conditions supported the initiation and growth. conditions include the operating stress, susceptible material typical for the pipe vintage, the area of coating disbondment and/or rocky outcrop shielding the pipe from corrosion protection, external corrosion serving as a crack raiser and the environmental conditions at the pipe surface promoting the development and growth pf the nnph scc (e.g. wet-dry conditions, neutral ph, bicarbonate ions).

NAME: GREAT LAKES GAS TRANSMISSION LIMITED PARTNERSHIP
NARRATIVE: ON JANUARY 12, 2024, SEVERE WEATHER INCLUDING HEAVY WINDS AND SNOW PASSED THROUGH THE GAYLORD, MICHIGAN AREA. WHEN THE POWER FAILURE ALARM WAS DETECTED AT 7:23 PM. EST, THE MONITORING CENTER CALLED THE TECHNICIAN ON SITE TO INVESTIGATE THE ALARM. THE TECHNICIAN COULD AUDIBLY HEAR BLOWING GAS AT 7:47 P.M. EST AND DISCOVERED NATURAL GAS WAS BEING RELEASED THROUGH THE UNIT 1101 BLOWDOWN STACK. IMMEDIATE ACTION WAS TAKEN BY VERIFYING NO FIRE EXISTED, A SECOND TECHNICIAN WAS DISPATCHED AND ASSISTED IN SAFELY ISOLATING THE GAS SOURCE BY CLOSING THE UNIT VALVE WHICH ENDED THE RELEASE AT 8:15 P.M. EST. UNINTENTIONAL GAS LOSS WAS CALCULATED TO 3.61 MILLION CUBIC FEET (MMCF).     NO PROPERTY DAMAGE, INJURIES OR MANDATORY EVACUATIONS WERE NEEDED. THE CAUSE OF THE UNINTENTIONAL RELEASE WAS ATTRIBUTED TO LOSS OF COMMERCIAL POWER AT THE STATION. THE BACKUP GENERATOR DID NOT START, AND THE VENT VALVE OPENED DUE TO THE LOSS OF CONTROL AIR PRESSURE.  THE VENT VALVE IS DESIGNED TO FAIL OPEN IN THE CASE OF LOW CONTROL AIR AND THE SUCTION AND DISCHARGE VALVES REMAINED IN THEIR CURRENT OPEN OPERATING STATE. NO OVERPRESSURE OCCURRED.     AFTER FURTHER INVESTIGATION OF THE AUXILIARY POWER UNIT (APU), IT WAS FOUND TWO LOOSE PRIMARY IGNITION WIRES CAUSED THE ENGINE TO BACKFIRE WHICH RESULTED IN A SMALL TEAR IN THE LEFT BANK SECONDARY FUEL REGULATOR DIAPHRAGM. A LOW HORSEPOWER CONDITION ENSUED. APU WAS REPAIRED AND PLACED BACK IN SERVICE ON JANUARY 19, 2024.    MODIFIED SECTIONS A5, G2 AND G6 PER PHMSA'S REQUEST.
narrative_clean: on january 12, 2024, severe weather including heavy winds and snow passed through the gaylord, michigan area. when the power failure alarm was detected at 7:23 pm. est, the monitoring center called the technician on site to investigate the alarm. the technician could audibly hear blowing gas at 7:47 p.m. est and discovered natural gas was being released through the unit 1101 blowdown stack. immediate action was taken by verifying no fire existed, a second technician was dispatched and assisted in safely isolating the gas source by closing the unit valve which ended the release at 8:15 p.m. est. unintentional gas loss was calculated to 3.61 million cubic feet (mmcf). no property damage, injuries or mandatory evacuations were needed. the cause of the unintentional release was attributed to loss of commercial power at the station. the backup generator did not start, and the vent valve opened due to the loss of control air pressure. the vent valve is designed to fail open in the case of low control air and the suction and discharge valves remained in their current open operating state. no overpressure occurred. after further investigation of the auxiliary power unit (apu), it was found two loose primary ignition wires caused the engine to backfire which resulted in a small tear in the left bank secondary fuel regulator diaphragm. a low horsepower condition ensued. apu was repaired and placed back in service on january 19, 2024. modified sections a5, g2 and g6 per phmsa's request.

NAME: MIDWESTERN GAS TRANSMISSION CO
NARRATIVE: ON 01/18/24, MIDWESTERN GAS TRANSMISSION PARIS COMPRESSOR STATION PERSONNEL WERE PERFORMING A ROUTINE INSPECTION OF THE STATION YARD PIPING WHEN THEY OBSERVED DAMAGE TO THE VALVE ACTUATOR ON MAINLINE VALVE 2113. AS THEY APPROACHED THE AREA, THEY NOTICED THE MAINLINE VALVE ACTUATOR HAD DISLODGED STRIKING THE MAINLINE VALVE 2113 BYPASS LINE. THE PARIS STATION WAS NOT RUNNING AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT. OPERATIONS CONFIRMED THAT THE DAMAGE DID NOT CAUSE A RELEASE. AN INVESTIGATION FOUND THAT WATER ENTERED THE INSIDE OF THE STEM EXTENSION HOUSING. BELOW ZERO TEMPERATURES CAUSED THIS WATER TO FREEZE AND BLOCK THE STEM EXTENSION VENT. DURING THE RESPONSE OPERATIONS FOUND A SMALL STEM LEAK ON MAINLINE VALVE 2113. THE STEM WAS LEAKING INTO THE VALVE EXTENSION HOUSING. THE FROZEN VENT DID NOT ALLOW THE PRESSURE TO EVACUATE THE STEM EXTENSION HOUSING WHICH CAUSED PRESSURE TO BUILD AND DISLODGE THE VALVE STEM EXTENSION. WHEN THE VALVE STEM DISLODGED, IT DAMAGED THE VALVE ACTUATOR AND BYPASS LINE. PROPERTY DAMAGE COSTS TO THE VALVE ACTUATOR AND BYPASS LINE EXCEEDED THE REPORTING THRESHOLD.
narrative_clean: on 01/18/24, midwestern gas transmission paris compressor station personnel were performing a routine inspection of the station yard piping when they observed damage to the valve actuator on mainline valve 2113. as they approached the area, they noticed the mainline valve actuator had dislodged striking the mainline valve 2113 bypass line. the paris station was not running at the time of the incident. operations confirmed that the damage did not cause a release. an investigation found that water entered the inside of the stem extension housing. below zero temperatures caused this water to freeze and block the stem extension vent. during the response operations found a small stem leak on mainline valve 2113. the stem was leaking into the valve extension housing. the frozen vent did not allow the pressure to evacuate the stem extension housing which caused pressure to build and dislodge the valve stem extension. when the valve stem dislodged, it damaged the valve actuator and bypass line. property damage costs to the valve actuator and bypass line exceeded the reporting threshold.

NAME: KINDER MORGAN TEJAS PIPELINE
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: KINDER MORGAN TEJAS GAS CONTROL RECEIVED A CALL FROM A HOMEOWNER OF A POTENTIAL NATURAL GAS LEAK.  KM OPERATIONS PERSONNEL RESPONDED AND VERIFIED THE PRESENCE OF GAS ABOVEGROUND ON ITS 202-600 LINE.  NOTIFICATIONS WERE MADE TO THE NATIONAL RESPONSE CENTER AND THE TXRRC.  OPERATIONS WERE DISPATCHED TO THE UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM VALVES AND LOCAL EMERGENCY RESPONDERS (HOUSTON FIRE DEPARTMENT) WERE CONTACTED AND DISPATCHED.  UPSTREAM AND DOWNSTREAM VALVES WERE CLOSED IN ORDER THAT THE PIPELINE SEGMENT COULD BE ISOLATED, AND THE PIPELINE BLOWN DOWN.  THE LEAK SITE WAS EXCAVATED, AND EVALUATION AND REPAIR OF THE LEAK BEGAN.  DURING EVALUATION THE CAUSE OF THE LEAK WAS DETERMINED TO BE FROM A CRACK AT A TAP WELD (TAP HAD PREVIOUSLY BEEN ABANDONED). THE REPAIR OF THE LEAK CONSISTED OF THE SEGMENT OF PIPE CONTAINING THE ABANDONED TAP BEING CUT OUT AND REPLACED WITH A PIECE OF STRAIGHT PIPE.  THE KINDER MORGAN METALLURGY DEPARTMENT IS CURRENTLY IN THE PROCESS OF COMPLETING A FAILURE ANALYSIS OF THE FAILED TAP CONNECTION.  UPON THE COMPLETION OF THE FAILURE ANALYSIS INVESTIGATION THIS REPORT WILL BE UPDATED AND FINALIZED.      ON MAY 9, 2024; KINDER MORGAN'S METALLURGICAL ENGINEER COMPLETED THE FAILURE ANALYSIS OF THE TAP CONNECTION.  THE FINAL CONCLUSIONS AS TO THE CAUSE OF THE FAILURE WERE: 1) THE LEAK WAS LOCATED AT THE TOE OF THE FILLET WELD ATTACHING A LOCALIZED SADDLE TO THE NPS 20 PIPE; 2) THE HOT TAP CONNECTION DID NOT HAVE A FULL ENCIRCLEMENT SADDLE, AND 3) THE FRACTURE WAS A DUCTILE OVERLOAD CAUSED BY A DOWNWARD BENDING MOMENT ON THE NPS 2 BRANCH.    PLEASE NOTE THAT CURRENT KINDER MORGAN ENGINEERING STANDARD E1100 WOULD NOT PERMIT NEW CONSTRUCTION WITH THIS NPS 2 ON NPS 20 HOT TAP CONFIGURATION WITH ONLY A LOCALIZED SADDLE AND NO FULL ENCIRCLEMENT SLEEVE.

NAME: TRANSCONTINENTAL GAS PIPE LINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: AN ACCIDENTAL IGNITION OCCURRED AT STATION 60 ON MAY 8, 2024, AN INTERSTATE TRANSMISSION COMPRESSOR STATION OPERATED BY TRANSCONTINENTAL PIPE LINE COMPANY, LLC (TRANSCO) NEAR JACKSON, LOUISIANA. AT THE TIME, STATION 60 WAS OFFLINE AND ISOLATED FROM OPERATING PIPELINES FOR SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE TO REPLACE INTERNAL VALVE COMPONENTS CONNECTING THE COMPRESSOR UNITS TO THE STATION'S COMMON SUCTION AND DISCHARGE HEADERS. THE INCIDENT HAPPENED AT 6:32 AM, JUST BEFORE SCHEDULED MAINTENANCE WORK WAS TO BEGIN FOR THAT DAY.   THE FACILITY'S CONSTRUCTION PROVIDED FOR SINGLE VALVE ISOLATION BETWEEN EACH PIPELINE AND FACILITY PIPING. WORK PLANS ANTICIPATED LEAKAGE AT THESE ISOLATION POINTS AND INCORPORATED AN AIR PURGE PLAN TO MITIGATE POTENTIAL FLAMMABLE ENVIRONMENTS WITHIN PIPING.     THE ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION DETERMINED THAT THE FOLLOWING CAUSES DIRECTLY LED TO THE CONSEQUENCES OF THIS INCIDENT:     1. FLAMMABLE MATERIAL (NATURAL GAS) LEAKED INTO THE STATION PIPING AROUND THE PROCESS ISOLATION BETWEEN THE STATION AND TRANSMISSION PIPELINES;  2. THE MITIGATIVE AIR FLOW DID NOT MAINTAIN FLAMMABLE GAS CONCENTRATION BELOW THE LEL;  3. THE MITIGATIVE AIR FLOW DRIED INTERNAL SLUDGE DEPOSITS INSIDE THE STATION PIPING;  4. SUSPECTED ACCUMULATION OF PYROPHORIC IRON SULFIDE IN THE INTERNAL SLUDGE DEPOSITS OF THE STATION PIPING IGNITED UPON EXPOSURE TO OXYGEN; AND  5. A PERSON WAS PRESENT WITHIN THE FIRE ZONE AT THE TIME OF THE ACCIDENTAL IGNITION.    TO PREVENT SIMILAR ISSUES FROM RECURRING, WILLIAMS IS COMMITTED TO FOLLOWING THE RECOMMENDATIONS DERIVED FROM THE ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS. THIS INCLUDES PROVIDING COMPREHENSIVE GUIDANCE AND CONDUCTING REFRESHER TRAINING FOR ALL PERSONNEL INVOLVED. BY REINFORCING THE KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS NECESSARY FOR SAFE OPERATIONS, WILLIAMS AIMS TO ENSURE THAT PERSONNEL ARE EQUIPPED TO RECOGNIZE POTENTIAL HAZARDS AND RESPOND APPROPRIATELY.    PHMSA REVIEWED WILLIAMS RETURN TO SERVICE PLAN AND APPROVED ON JUNE 18TH, 2024. WILLIAMS STATION 60 RETURNED TO SERVICE ON JUNE 22ND AT 9:55 AM
narrative_clean: an accidental ignition occurred at station 60 on may 8, 2024, an interstate transmission compressor station operated by transcontinental pipe line company, llc (transco) near jackson, louisiana. at the time, station 60 was offline and isolated from operating pipelines for scheduled maintenance to replace internal valve components connecting the compressor units to the station's common suction and discharge headers. the incident happened at 6:32 am, just before scheduled maintenance work was to begin for that day. the facility's construction provided for single valve isolation between each pipeline and facility piping. work plans anticipated leakage at these isolation points and incorporated an air purge plan to mitigate potential flammable environments within piping. the root cause investigation determined that the following causes directly led to the consequences of this incident: 1. flammable material (natural gas) leaked into the station piping around the process isolation between the station and transmission pipelines; 2. the mitigative air flow did not maintain flammable gas concentration below the lel; 3. the mitigative air flow dried internal sludge deposits inside the station piping; 4. suspected accumulation of pyrophoric iron sulfide in the internal sludge deposits of the station piping ignited upon exposure to oxygen; and 5. a person was present within the fire zone at the time of the accidental ignition. to prevent similar issues from recurring, williams is committed to following the recommendations derived from the root cause analysis. this includes providing comprehensive guidance and conducting refresher training for all personnel involved. by reinforcing the knowledge and skills necessary for safe operations, williams aims to ensure that personnel are equipped to recognize potential hazards and respond appropriately. phmsa reviewed williams return to service plan and approved on june 18th, 2024. williams station 60 returned to service on june 22nd at 9:55 am

NAME: ENERFIN GATHERING LLC
NARRATIVE: DURING ROUTINE PIGGING OPERATION TO REMOVE HYDROCARBON LIQUIDS AND WATER FROM A 60-PSIG GAS GATHERING PIPELINE, THE FLUIDS WERE DECANTED IN A CONTROLLED MANNER INTO A TEMPORARY ATMOSPHERIC STORAGE (FRAC) TANK. OPERATING PROCEDURES DID NOT ADDRESS THE NEED TO ESTABLISH A SAFETY ZONE (VISUAL WARNINGS AND WINDSOCKS) AROUND THE PIPELINE PIGGING OPERATION AREA TO HELP TO ELIMINATE RANDOM IGNITION SOURCES IN AN AREA EXPECTED TO HAVE TEMPORARY EXPOSURE TO HYDROCARBON VAPORS. ULTIMATELY, IT WAS A VEHICLE WHICH WAS PARKED TOO CLOSE TO THE WORK AREA WHICH PROVIDED THE IGNITION SOURCE WHEN AN EMPLOYEE ENTERED THE VEHICLE AND TURNED THE IGNITION KEY. THE RELEASE OF HYDROCARBON VAPORS WAS THE EXPECTED RESULT OF THE CONTROLLED DEPRESSURIZING OF A STREAM OF HYDROCARBON LIQUIDS INTO AN ATMOSPHERIC STORAGE VESSEL, WHICH HAD NO MEANS OF VAPOR CONTAINMENT. ADDITIONALLY, A VAPOR CONTROL AND DISCHARGE PLAN WAS NOT UTILIZED DURING THE PROCESS. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE FIRE WAS A FAILURE OF OPERATING PROCEDURES IN ALLOWING A POTENTIAL SOURCE OF IGNITION (A VEHICLE) TO BE LOCATED WITHIN AN AREA EXPECTED TO BE TEMPORARILY EXPOSED TO EVOLVED HYDROCARBON VAPORS. THIS INCIDENT WAS NOT THE RESULT OF ANY PIPELINE MATERIAL FAILURE, ABNORMAL OPERATING CONDITIONS (I.E., OVERPRESSURE CONDITION), OR INCIDENTAL THIRD-PARTY DAMAGE TO THE PIPELINE FACILITIES.

NARRATIVE: ON MARCH 2, 2025, AT APPROXIMATELY 16:03, LINE SM-116 WAS SUBJECT TO AN UNINTENDED RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS TO ATMOSPHERE DUE TO A FAILURE IN THE BODY OF THE PIPELINE. THE PIPELINE FAILURE WAS NOTED BY SCADA ALARMS AND WAS ACKNOWLEDGED AND RESPONDED TO BY COLUMBIAS GAS CONTROLLER. FIELD OPERATIONS PERSONNEL WERE NOTIFIED AND RESPONDED TO THE FAILED PIPELINES LOCATION FOR INVESTIGATION. UPON RECEIPT THE FAILED PIPELINE EVIDENCE WAS INSPECTED AND PRESENTED NO VISUAL INDICATIONS TO EITHER EXTERNAL OR INTERNAL CORROSION. METALLURGICAL EXAMINATION DETERMINED THAT TOPSIDE MECHANICAL DAMAGE WAS THE DIRECT CAUSE OF THE SM-116 RUPTURE. MULTIPLE DENTS AND GOUGES WERE FOUND ON THE TOP OF THE PIPE MOST LIKELY CAUSED BY MACHINERY, SUCH AS AN EXCAVATOR. THERE WAS NO EVIDENCE OF FATIGUE CRACK GROWTH,  SCC, OR MATERIAL DEFECTS AS CONTRIBUTING FACTORS. IN ADDITION, A ROOT CAUSE FAILURE ANALYSIS REPORT WAS COMPLETED BY AN INDEPENDENT THIRD PARTY DETERMINING THE DIRECT CAUSE OF THE SM-116 RUPTURE WAS DUE TO THIRD PARTY MECHANICAL DAMAGE. narrative_clean: on march 2, 2025, at approximately 16:03, line sm-116 was subject to an unintended release of natural gas to atmosphere due to a failure in the body of the pipeline. line sm-116, a carbon steel transmission pipeline with 16-inch nps (nominal pipe size), 0.281-inch wall thickness at location of failure is operated and maintained by columbia gas transmission llc (columbia), a subsidiary of tc energy. the pipeline failure was noted by scada alarms and was acknowledged and responded to by columbias gas controller. field operations personnel were notified and responded to the failed pipelines location for investigation. columbia field operations personnel completed the isolation of the failed segment of sm-116 by closing two mainline valves. the failed pipeline evidence was removed and transported to a metallurgical failure analysis (mfa) laboratory for further analysis. upon receipt the failed pipeline evidence was inspected and presented no visual indications to either external or internal corrosion. metallurgical examination determined that topside mechanical damage was the direct cause of the sm-116 rupture. multiple dents and gouges were found on the top of the pipe most likely caused by machinery, such as an excavator. there was no evidence of fatigue crack growth, scc, or material defects as contributing factors. in addition, a root cause failure analysis report was completed by an independent third party determining the direct cause of the sm-116 rupture was due to third party mechanical damage. lessons learned and recommendations were proposed to improve working relationships with state and/or local authorities to help with outreach to businesses that have an enhanced third-party external interference (tpei) risk based on equipment used onsite and the activities conducted. all times are reported in eastern standard time.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: ON JUNE 18, 2025, NATURAL GAS VENTED TO THE ATMOSPHERE THROUGH BLOWDOWN STACKS AT TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE'S (TGP) COMPRESSOR STATION 856 IN SAVANNAH, TENNESSEE. THE VENTING OCCURRED WHEN THE STATION'S EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN (ESD) SYSTEM WAS ACTIVATED DUE TO A SHORTED WIRE ASSOCIATED WITH THE DISCHARGE-SIDE VALVE. THE WIRING FAULT CAUSED THE CONTROL SYSTEM TO INDICATE THAT THE VALVE WAS IN THE CLOSED POSITION WHEN IT WAS ACTUALLY OPEN. AS A RESULT, THE SIDE-GATE VALVES BEGAN TO OPEN BASED ON THE FALSE CLOSED INDICATION FROM THE DISCHARGE-SIDE VALVE. FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT INVESTIGATION, THE PLC CABINET WAS RELOCATED TO A HIGHER ELEVATION TO REDUCE THE POTENTIAL FOR WATER INTRUSION AND PREVENT FUTURE WIRING-RELATED FAILURES.
narrative_clean: on june 18, 2025, natural gas vented to the atmosphere through blowdown stacks at tennessee gas pipeline's (tgp) compressor station 856 in savannah, tennessee. the venting occurred when the station's emergency shutdown (esd) system was activated due to a shorted wire associated with the discharge-side valve. the wiring fault caused the control system to indicate that the valve was in the closed position when it was actually open. as a result, the side-gate valves began to open based on the false closed indication from the discharge-side valve. following the incident investigation, the plc cabinet was relocated to a higher elevation to reduce the potential for water intrusion and prevent future wiring-related failures.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: AT 14:05 HOURS ON AUGUST 6, 2025, A NORTHERN NATURAL GAS OPERATIONS TECHNICIAN DISCOVERED A RELIEF VALVE VENTING AT THE MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA NO. 1R (STATION NO. 753160) IN CARVER, MINNESOTA.  THE OPERATIONS TEAM CONTACTED THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT AND SHERIFFS DEPARTMENT TO SUPPORT WITH THE CLOSING OF COUNTY ROAD 40.  THE ROAD WAS SUCCESSFULLY CLOSED AT 14:24 HOURS UNTIL THE OPERATIONS TEAM WAS ABLE TO DIVERT FLOW THROUGH THE STATION BYPASS  AND SUCCESSFULLY STOPPED THE RELIEF VALVE VENTING AT 14:28 HOURS.  THE COUNTY ROAD WAS THEN REOPENED AT 14:35 HOURS.      DURING THE ONSITE INSPECTION OF THE RELIEF VALVE THE OPERATIONS TEAM, IT WAS BELIEVED THAT THE RELIEF VALVE AND RELIEF PILOT VALVE WERE DAMAGED BY DEBRIS PREVENTING IT FROM RESEATING AND CLOSING.  THE DEBRIS WAS SUSPECTED TO HAVE ORIGINATED FROM RECENT NEARBY CONSTRUCTION ON THE PIPELINE.  WHEN THE REGULATOR STRAINERS WERE EXAMINED, THEY WERE FOUND TO HAVE BECOME DISLODGED, RELEASING ANY DEBRIS THEY HELD.    THE RELIEF VALVE AND RELIEF VALVE PILOT WERE REBUILT ON-SITE AND VERIFIED FOR PROPER OPERATION.  AT 17:00 HOURS ON AUGUST 7, 2025, THE STATION WAS PUT BACK INTO NORMAL OPERATIONS.    FOLLOWING THE INCIDENT, THE RELIEF VALVE PILOT WAS SENT TO THE VENDOR TO BE EXAMINED BY A MATERIAL SPECIALIST.  THE SPECIALIST FOUND THAT THE PILOT DISK HAD WEAKENED CAUSING THE PILOT TO FAIL OPEN DAMAGING THE RELIEF VALVE BOOT DUE TO THE HIGH VELOCITY OF GAS VENTING THROUGH THE RELIEF VALVE.  THIS STYLE OF PILOT DISK WAS KNOWN BY SPECIALIST TO WEAKEN OVER TIME, AND IT IS NO LONGER BEING USED BY THE VENDOR.  NORTHERN NATURAL GAS IS LOOKING AT REPLACING ALL PILOT DISKS OF THIS STYLE.
narrative_clean: at 14:05 hours on august 6, 2025, a northern natural gas operations technician discovered a relief valve venting at the minneapolis, minnesota no. 1r (station no. 753160) in carver, minnesota. the operations team contacted the local fire department and sheriffs department to support with the closing of county road 40. the road was successfully closed at 14:24 hours until the operations team was able to divert flow through the station bypass and successfully stopped the relief valve venting at 14:28 hours. the county road was then reopened at 14:35 hours. during the onsite inspection of the relief valve the operations team, it was believed that the relief valve and relief pilot valve were damaged by debris preventing it from reseating and closing. the debris was suspected to have originated from recent nearby construction on the pipeline. when the regulator strainers were examined, they were found to have become dislodged, releasing any debris they held. the relief valve and relief valve pilot were rebuilt on-site and verified for proper operation. at 17:00 hours on august 7, 2025, the station was put back into normal operations. following the incident, the relief valve pilot was sent to the vendor to be examined by a material specialist. the specialist found that the pilot disk had weakened causing the pilot to fail open damaging the relief valve boot due to the high velocity of gas venting through the relief valve. this style of pilot disk was known by specialist to weaken over time, and it is no longer being used by the vendor. northern natural gas is looking at replacing all pilot disks of this style.

NAME: EASTERN GAS TRANSMISSION AND STORAGE, INC.
NARRATIVE: ON 9/12/2025 AT APPROXIMATELY 19:32, UP-24 RUPTURED AT STATION 125+05 NEAR THE DRIP AND LAUNCHER / RECEIVER AT THE UW-204 WELL PAD IN FORBES STATE FOREST WHICH IS LOCATED WEST OF FARMINGTON, PA IN FAYETTE COUNTY. GAS CONTROL RECEIVED INITIAL INDICATION OF THE RUPTURE FROM SCADA PRESSURE DROP ALARMS ON UP-2, UP-5, AND UP-7 AT 19:32. UP-24 IS AN 8 INCH DIAMETER TRANSMISSION PIPELINE IN STORAGE FUNCTION APPROXIMATELY 2.3 MILES LONG AND TRANSPORTS GAS BETWEEN OTHER TRANSMISSION PIPELINES IN STORAGE FUNCTION AND UW-204 WHICH IS AN UNDERGROUND STORAGE WELL IN NORTH SUMMIT STORAGE. THE MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE OPERATING PRESSURE OF UP-24 IS 3377 PSIG. UP-24 WAS IN NORMAL OPERATION WITH AN OPERATING PRESSURE OF 3176 PSIG AND NO FLOW WHEN THE INCIDENT OCCURRED. AT APPROXIMATELY 20:20, OPERATIONS PERSONNEL CALLED GAS CONTROL AND CONFIRMED THAT NATURAL GAS WAS BLOWING IN NORTH SUMMIT STORAGE. FAYETTE COUNTY 911 CALLED GAS CONTROL AT APPROXIMATELY 20:31 AND PROVIDED A SIMILAR NOTIFICATION. OPERATIONS PERSONNEL MANUALLY CLOSED VALVE UP-24 UPSTREAM OF UP-24 AT APPROXIMATELY 20:55 AND MANUALLY CLOSED THE MASTER GATE VALVE AND LEAD LINES ON UW-204 DOWNSTREAM OF UP-24 AT APPROXIMATELY 21:20 TO COMPLETE THE ISOLATION OF UP-24. GAS CONTROL ALSO INITIATED COMMANDS TO REMOTELY CLOSE VALVES UP-5 AND UP-116 TO SUPPORT THE ISOLATION OF UP-24 AT APPROXIMATELY 20:57. GAS CEASED BLOWING FROM UP-24 AT APPROXIMATELY 21:29. THE RUPTURE RESULTED IN THE LONGITUDINAL AND THEN CIRCUMFERENTIAL FAILURE OF PIPE GOING TO THE DRIP; AN APPROXIMATELY 25 FT BY 30 FT HOLE IN THE GROUND APPROXIMATELY 12 FT TO 15 FT DEEP; APPROXIMATELY 14 FT OF PIPE FOLDING UP AND COMING OUT OF THE GROUND; APPROXIMATELY 1.5 FT OF PIPE BEING EJECTED APPROXIMATELY 73 FT AWAY FROM THE HOLE; DAMAGE TO THE DRIP AND ASSOCIATED PIPING; DAMAGE TO THE LAUNCHER / RECEIVER AND ASSOCIATED PIPING; DAMAGE TO A NEARBY ABOVEGROUND BRINE STORAGE TANK AT THE UW-204 WELL PAD AND ASSOCIATED PIPING; APPROXIMATELY 26,067 MCF GAS LOSS FROM UP-24; APPROXIMATELY 3,092 MCF OF GAS LOSS FROM UW-204; AND APPROXIMATELY 0.05 BARRELS OF BRINE SPILLED TO THE GROUND. THE GAS DID NOT IGNITE AND THERE WERE NO FIRES, INJURIES, FATALITIES, OR EVACUATIONS. INITIAL NOTIFICATION (#1442611) WAS MADE TO THE NRC ON 9/12/2025 AT 20:45. FOLLOW UP NOTIFICATION (#1442677) WAS MADE TO THE NRC ON 9/13/2025 AT 20:50. FOUR PIECES OF UP-24 PIPE WERE CUT-OUT AT THE RUPTURE AND WERE SENT TO KIEFNER & ASSOCIATES FOR FAILURE ANALYSIS. THE FAILURE ANALYSIS REPORT FROM KIEFNER WAS COMPLETED AND IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT INTERNAL CORROSION WAS THE PRIMARY CAUSE. AS A PRECAUTIONARY MEASURE, THE INTEGRITY OF THE UW-204 WELLHEAD AND ANNULAR VENT WERE INSPECTED ON 9/13/2025 AND IT WAS CONFIRMED THAT UW-204 COULD BE SAFELY RETURNED TO SERVICE ONCE THE REMEDIATION ACTIONS FOR UP-24 WERE COMPLETED AND UP-24 WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE. THE ISOLATION OF UP-24 REMAINED IN EFFECT UNTIL THE FOLLOWING REMEDIATION ACTIONS WERE COMPLETED: THE SECTION OF UP-24 CONTAINING THE RUPTURE WAS REPLACED WHICH INVOLVED THE REPLACEMENT OF APPROXIMATELY 180 FT OF 8 INCH PIPE; THE DRIP AND ASSOCIATED PIPING WERE REPLACED; THE NEARBY ABOVEGROUND BRINE STORAGE TANK AND ASSOCIATED PIPING WERE REPAIRED; AND THE SOIL WHERE THE BRINE SPILLED WAS CLEANED UP. IN ADDITION TO THE REMEDIAL ACTIONS ABOVE, THE UW-204 SITE WAS RECONFIGURED TO ALLOW ADDITIONAL PIPING TO BE IN-LINE INSPECTED IN THE FUTURE, IMPROVE THE FUNCTIONALITY OF THE DRIP, AND ADDITIONAL INSPECTIONS OF NORTH SUMMIT STORAGE WERE PERFORMED. THE ESTIMATED COST OF THE RECONFIGURATION OF THE UW-204 SITE AND ADDITIONAL INSPECTIONS OF NORTH SUMMIT STORAGE WAS $2,506,965.  THE LAUNCHER / RECEIVER AND ASSOCIATED PIPING ARE SCHEDULED TO BE REPLACED IN 2026 SO AS TO BE LOCATED CLOSER TO UW-204 TO ALLOW ADDITIONAL PIPING TO BE IN-LINE INSPECTED IN THE FUTURE. UP-24 WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON 12/10/2025 AT APPROXIMATELY 11:30.
narrative_clean: on 9/12/2025 at approximately 19:32, up-24 ruptured at station 125+05 near the drip and launcher / receiver at the uw-204 well pad in forbes state forest which is located west of farmington, pa in fayette county. gas control received initial indication of the rupture from scada pressure drop alarms on up-2, up-5, and up-7 at 19:32. up-24 is an 8 inch diameter transmission pipeline in storage function approximately 2.3 miles long and transports gas between other transmission pipelines in storage function and uw-204 which is an underground storage well in north summit storage. the maximum allowable operating pressure of up-24 is 3377 psig. up-24 was in normal operation with an operating pressure of 3176 psig and no flow when the incident occurred. at approximately 20:20, operations personnel called gas control and confirmed that natural gas was blowing in north summit storage. fayette county 911 called gas control at approximately 20:31 and provided a similar notification. operations personnel manually closed valve up-24 upstream of up-24 at approximately 20:55 and manually closed the master gate valve and lead lines on uw-204 downstream of up-24 at approximately 21:20 to complete the isolation of up-24. gas control also initiated commands to remotely close valves up-5 and up-116 to support the isolation of up-24 at approximately 20:57. gas ceased blowing from up-24 at approximately 21:29. the rupture resulted in the longitudinal and then circumferential failure of pipe going to the drip; an approximately 25 ft by 30 ft hole in the ground approximately 12 ft to 15 ft deep; approximately 14 ft of pipe folding up and coming out of the ground; approximately 1.5 ft of pipe being ejected approximately 73 ft away from the hole; damage to the drip and associated piping; damage to the launcher / receiver and associated piping; damage to a nearby aboveground brine storage tank at the uw-204 well pad and associated piping; approximately 26,067 mcf gas loss from up-24; approximately 3,092 mcf of gas loss from uw-204; and approximately 0.05 barrels of brine spilled to the ground. the gas did not ignite and there were no fires, injuries, fatalities, or evacuations. initial notification (#1442611) was made to the nrc on 9/12/2025 at 20:45. follow up notification (#1442677) was made to the nrc on 9/13/2025 at 20:50. four pieces of up-24 pipe were cut-out at the rupture and were sent to kiefner & associates for failure analysis. the failure analysis report from kiefner was completed and it was confirmed that internal corrosion was the primary cause. as a precautionary measure, the integrity of the uw-204 wellhead and annular vent were inspected on 9/13/2025 and it was confirmed that uw-204 could be safely returned to service once the remediation actions for up-24 were completed and up-24 was returned to service. the isolation of up-24 remained in effect until the following remediation actions were completed: the section of up-24 containing the rupture was replaced which involved the replacement of approximately 180 ft of 8 inch pipe; the drip and associated piping were replaced; the nearby aboveground brine storage tank and associated piping were repaired; and the soil where the brine spilled was cleaned up. in addition to the remedial actions above, the uw-204 site was reconfigured to allow additional piping to be in-line inspected in the future, improve the functionality of the drip, and additional inspections of north summit storage were performed. the estimated cost of the reconfiguration of the uw-204 site and additional inspections of north summit storage was $2,506,965. the launcher / receiver and associated piping are scheduled to be replaced in 2026 so as to be located closer to uw-204 to allow additional piping to be in-line inspected in the future. up-24 was returned to service on 12/10/2025 at approximately 11:30.

NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
CAUSE_DETAILS: ORIGINAL MANUFACTURING-RELATED (NOT GIRTH WELD OR OTHER WELDS FORMED IN THE FIELD)
NARRATIVE: ON OCTOBER 5TH, 2025 AT 12:10 P.M. GAS CONTROL RECEIVED A CALL FROM A LANDOWNER REPORTING A LEAK IN AN ET ROW. OPERATIONS WAS DISPATCHED AT 12:15PM AND CONFIRMED AT 2:31 P.M. THAT THE LINE WAS OUR 1090 SUGAR VALLEY PIPELINE. THE LINE WAS ISOLATED BY VALVE CLOSURE BY 3:56 P.M.    THE NEXT MORNING OCTOBER 6TH 2025 AT 11:22 A.M. CALCULATIONS CONFIRMED THE INCIDENT TO BE REPORTABLE, DUE TO THE GAS LOSS EXCEEDING THE REPORTING THRESHOLD.   PERMANENT REPAIRS (PIPE REPLACEMENT) WERE COMPLETED BY OCTOBER 10TH 2025. THE LINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE ON OCTOBER 24TH, 2025 AT 2:00 P.M. THE PIPE HAS BEEN SENT TO A LAB WHERE THE CAUSE IS PENDING THE RESULTS OF THE METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS.    **THE RESULTS OF THE METALLURGICAL ANALYSIS DETERMINED THAT THE CAUSE WAS FROM AN ORIGINAL MANUFACTURING DEFECT IN THE LAP SEAM WELD.    TO PREVENT THIS FROM REOCCURRING THE 1090 SUGAR VALLEY 12IN FIELD WILL UNDERGO A PERMANENT MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE OPERATING PRESSURE (MAOP) REDUCTION TO TWO-HUNDRED AND FIFTY (250) PSIG.  THE ORIGINAL MAOP WAS ESTABLISHED AT FIVE-HUNDRED (500) PSI; FOLLOWING THE RUPTURE EVENT, THE LINE WAS RETURNED TO SERVICE AT A TEMPORARY MAOP OF THREE-HUNDRED AND SIXTY (360) PSIG. AFTER FURTHER COMMERCIAL ANALYSIS, IT WAS DETERMINED THE MAOP COULD BE FURTHER REDUCED TO 250 PSIG. THIS MITIGATIVE MEASURE TO PERMANENTLY REDUCE WILL DECREASE THE MAXIMUM ALLOWABLE TENSILE HOOP STRESS THAT THIS PIPE SEGMENT MAY EXPERIENCE, WHICH WILL REDUCE BY HALF THE RISK OF INTERNAL PRESSURE THAT COULD AFFECT THE PIPE SEAM.
narrative_clean: on october 5th, 2025 at 12:10 p.m. gas control received a call from a landowner reporting a leak in an et row. operations was dispatched at 12:15pm and confirmed at 2:31 p.m. that the line was our 1090 sugar valley pipeline. the line was isolated by valve closure by 3:56 p.m. the next morning october 6th 2025 at 11:22 a.m. calculations confirmed the incident to be reportable, due to the gas loss exceeding the reporting threshold. permanent repairs (pipe replacement) were completed by october 10th 2025. the line was returned to service on october 24th, 2025 at 2:00 p.m. the pipe has been sent to a lab where the cause is pending the results of the metallurgical analysis. **the results of the metallurgical analysis determined that the cause was from an original manufacturing defect in the lap seam weld. to prevent this from reoccurring the 1090 sugar valley 12in field will undergo a permanent maximum allowable operating pressure (maop) reduction to two-hundred and fifty (250) psig. the original maop was established at five-hundred (500) psi; following the rupture event, the line was returned to service at a temporary maop of three-hundred and sixty (360) psig. after further commercial analysis, it was determined the maop could be further reduced to 250 psig. this mitigative measure to permanently reduce will decrease the maximum allowable tensile hoop stress that this pipe segment may experience, which will reduce by half the risk of internal pressure that could affect the pipe seam.
